title: Pierce Brosnan backs 'Fantastic Beasts' star for next James Bond, predicts fans will be 'blown away'
summary: Pierce Brosnan singled out Callum Turner as a standout among the actors being considered for the next James Bond role in a Vanity Fair interview.
story: Former Bond girl Alison Papworth shares why she wants the next 007 to stay true to the books as speculation swirls over the role.
Pierce Brosnan is throwing in his two cents into the conversation regarding who should be chosen to play the next James Bond, nearly 25 years after he last played the iconic character.

During a recent interview with Vanity Fair, the 73-year-old actor said he is following along with the public as "an audience member," adding he is just as "eager" as everyone else "to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history." He did, however, give one actor a special shoutout.

"All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire," he said. "Callum, Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong. They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men."
While he doesn't know who will take on the iconic role next, Brosnan wishes whoever is chosen "the very best of life and strength and courage."
Brosnan wishes whoever takes over as the next James Bond strength. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)
FORMER BOND GIRL SAYS NEXT 007 SHOULD BE 'ANOTHER GORGEOUS MAN' AS JAMES BOND DECISION

Brosnan first appeared as agent 007 in the 1995 movie, "GoldenEye," having taken over the reins from Timothy Dalton. He appeared in his final Bond movie in 2002 with the release of "Die Another Day," and was replaced by Daniel Craig in the 2006 movie, "Casino Royale."
Craig starred as James Bond in six films, before hanging up his badge following the release of "No Time to Die" in 2021.
Brosnan began his tenure as James Bond in 1995 with the release of "GoldenEye." (Keith Hamshere/Getty Images)
"You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond," Brosnan said.
In addition to a new actor playing Bond, the film is also getting a new director in Denis Villeneuve, who will be taking over the franchise, which excites Brosnan.

When speaking with GQ about the mental and physical load of playing the character in September 2022, he nonchalantly explained, "You get chipped, you get nicked, you pull muscles, you get stitched up."
Brosnan also touched on the physical toll of playing James Bond. (Mike Marsland/WireImage)

title: King Charles' 'short fuse' on display in viral downpour as Queen Camilla gets umbrella first: expert
summary: King Charles III was left drenched after aides failed to provide an umbrella during a downpour in Antigua, while Queen Camilla was quickly sheltered.
story: The monarch got soaked during a celebration of Antigua and Barbuda’s 45th anniversary of independence at Sir Vivian Richards Stadium. Copyright: Thomson Reuters. Courtesy of ABS TV Radio.
King Charles III was left royally soaked — and his patience appeared to dry up faster than his suit.

The British monarch was caught without an umbrella as the skies opened on Nov. 1 during a celebration at Sir Vivian Richards Stadium marking Antigua and Barbuda's 45th anniversary of independence. Charles and his wife, Queen Camilla, were attending the parade during their royal tour of the Caribbean when the weather took a sudden turn.

As heavy rain pelted the royal couple, Camilla was quickly handed an umbrella and hurried toward shelter. Charles, however, was left exposed to the elements, getting more drenched by the second and appearing increasingly exasperated.
KING CHARLES’ ‘JUST GIVE US A RING!’ QUIP LEADS VIRAL MOMENTS FROM ROYAL US TOUR WITH QUEEN CAMILLA

King Charles III arrives in the rain for the annual Independence Ceremonial Parade, marking 45 years of Antigua and Barbuda's independence, at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026, in St John's, Antigua and Barbuda. (Aaron Chown - Pool/Getty Images)

After spotting his wife walking away beneath an umbrella, the 77-year-old threw his hands into the air and repeatedly waved at royal aides, apparently calling for an umbrella of his own as rain soaked his suit.
Help eventually arrived, but not before Charles was drenched. By the time an aide handed him an umbrella, the king was already soaking wet.

King Charles III walks in the rain as he attends a military parade marking Antigua and Barbuda's 45th Independence anniversary at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in Antigua and Barbuda on Nov. 1, 2026. (Pool/AFP via Getty Images)

"King Charles has historically had a short fuse," royal commentator Meredith Constant told Fox News Digital. "What we see is that when he is under immense pressure and something seemingly small goes awry, like the pen incident, he loses his cool. In the situation with the umbrella, King Charles had every right to be annoyed with his aides. He's in his late 70s, living with cancer; his wife was immediately handed an umbrella; this was a downpour, not a light drizzle."
WATCH: KING CHARLES CAUGHT IN DOWNPOUR DURING ROYAL TOUR

"One of the reasons Charles and Camilla work is that she balances him out," Constant said. "She can laugh it off, share a funny aside; she has the ability to let things roll off her shoulders in a way Charles never has. Charles and Camilla function much more like a unit, particularly because Camilla never tries to compete for the limelight."

Camilla couldn't hold back her laughter when she rejoined her husband on the dais after the rain eased. The couple chuckled at the mishap. "I've started growing watercress on my trousers," Charles joked, according to the Evening Standard.

Queen Camilla gestures in the rain as she attends the annual Independence Ceremonial Parade with King Charles III at Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in St. John's, Antigua and Barbuda, Nov. 1, 2026. (Getty Images)

"The umbrella incident was in stark contrast to the public composure, restraint and emotional discipline demonstrated by Queen Elizabeth," British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "Yet 'all's well that ends well’ as the giggles King Charles and Queen Camilla displayed after the rain saved the day."
Queen Elizabeth II attends the Out-Sourcing Inc. Royal Windsor Cup polo match at Guards Polo Club in Egham, England, on July 11, 2021. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"The humor King Charles displayed at the moment, without any advice or counsel from courtiers, was immensely significant as it demonstrated he can handle challenges with grace, dignity and deflect with humor," she said.
But Constant said the soaking threatened more than Charles' carefully tailored suit.
King Charles III was in a stormy mood during the rainfall. (Getty Images)

"There's a lot of consideration as to what his legacy will look like," she said. "He certainly doesn't want images of him looking like a drowned rat in the archives, especially when there are large discussions happening about the future of the Commonwealth. Image is everything. This situation should never have happened."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
King Charles III is seen here with the umbrella that he was waiting for. (Getty Images)
Fordwich said the mishap became known as "Brolly-gate" in the U.K. "Brolly" is a common informal term for an umbrella.
"Queen Elizabeth II maintained a firmer distinction between her private reactions and her public responsibilities," Fordwich said, referring to the king's late mother.
Queen Camilla shelters from the rain under an umbrella. (Getty Images)

"She was from the generation which placed emphasis on public reserve. The immediacy of modern social media means unexpected incidents like this rocket around the world in minutes. The king is more visibly expressive, at times impatient, occasionally humorous and way more willing to let audiences see his immediate reactions than his mother."
Queen Elizabeth II attends a ceremony to mark her official birthday at Windsor Castle on June 13, 2020, in Windsor, England. (Toby Melville - WPA Pool/Getty Images)
Christopher Andersen, author of "The King," previously told Fox News Digital that sources had described Charles as having a short fuse in his younger years.

"He's very moody, very temperamental," Andersen said. "He has a volcanic temper. Camilla has always been a calming influence, and since he became king, Charles has mellowed considerably. That doesn't mean he's lost his edge entirely, by any means. When he is displeased by something, he lets his staff know it in no uncertain terms. They feel the royal heat."
King Charles III signs the visitors' book as Queen Camilla watches at Hillsborough Castle in Belfast on Sept. 13, 2022, during his visit to Northern Ireland. (Pool/AFP via Getty Images)
A Buckingham Palace spokesperson previously told Fox News Digital they don’t comment on books.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
"The King: The Life of Charles III" by Christopher Andersen is out now. (Gallery Books)

Following his mother's death in September 2022, Charles appeared frustrated with a leaking pen during a visit to Northern Ireland. He told an aide, "I can't bear this bloody thing! Every stinking time." A pen was quickly handed to Camilla to complete the signing during the royal ceremony.
Fordwich said the king's reaction to the downpour contrasted with the late queen's reputation for maintaining her public composure. Constant agreed.
Queen Elizabeth II watches from the balcony of Buckingham Palace during the Trooping the Colour parade in London on June 2, 2022. (Jonathan Brady/WPA Pool/Getty Images)

"Queen Elizabeth was much better at embodying the 'keep calm, carry on' tradition, especially in public," she said. "That was never going to be Charles. These moments stand out because they are in such stark contrast to Queen Elizabeth. King Charles is very aware that he is viewed as a transitional monarch, and he wants to leave his mark."
King Charles is seen here with his mother, Queen Elizabeth II, before her death in 2022 at age 96. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
Royal experts agreed Charles has been navigating mounting pressure, as the Caribbean tour unfolded amid renewed calls from regional leaders for the U.K. to address slavery reparations.

On Nov. 3, the king called the transatlantic slave trade a "shameful chapter of history" during a speech at the official opening of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda. While Charles said it "still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth," he did not apologize, The Associated Press reported.

King Charles III greets locals holding national flags during a visit to Nelson's Dockyard, a historic naval base established in 1725, in St. John's, Antigua and Barbuda, on Nov. 2, 2026. (Pool/AFP via Getty Images)

According to The Associated Press, Charles said he was seeking ways to address past wrongs by improving access to education, investing in jobs, encouraging intra-Commonwealth trade and promoting climate resilience.

"We are so used to perfection that the media salivates over leaky pens," royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital about the umbrella mishap.

Britain's King Charles III reacts after joking while delivering a speech at an official dinner and reception during the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Soldier's Bay near St. John's, Antigua and Barbuda, on Nov. 3, 2026. (Pool/AFP via Getty Images)

"The thunderstorm, of course, should have been anticipated," he said. "And given that King Charles is fighting cancer, no wonder he needed an umbrella. Queen Camilla realized her umbrella was not large enough to cover the king as well and duly behaved with dignity. Afterward, they both laughed about it, which is very British. Neither would have thought it funny at the time and small wonder. It’s unlikely to be repeated."
The soggy snafu drew international headlines, but Charles refused to let it rain on his parade.
King Charles III and Queen Camilla prepare to depart from VC Bird International Airport in St. John's, Antigua and Barbuda, on Nov. 4, 2026. (Pool/AFP via Getty Images)
During a dinner he and Camilla hosted for Commonwealth leaders, Charles joked about the varied climates across the organization's 56 member countries.

"It is one of the few organizations able to unite countries famous for snow, countries famous for deserts, and, most of all, countries whose citizens are utterly convinced they enjoy perfect weather all year round," he said, according to People magazine.

King Charles III and Antigua and Barbuda's Prime Minister Gaston Browne attend an official dinner and reception during the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Soldier's Bay near St. John's, Antigua and Barbuda, on Nov. 3, 2026. (Pool/AFP via Getty Images)
"Although perhaps part of my role as Head of the Commonwealth is to provide an umbrella for you all!" he added with a smile.

"Sometimes that requires not talking about it and just moving on through," he said. "And sometimes it requires sitting down and talking about it a little bit, saying, 'Hey, we need to check in a little bit and see where we're at now that everything's changing.'"
He went on to say that "points of change in a marriage" can come "regularly throughout a long marriage," and these can often be "the most dangerous parts, I think, for a marriage."

title: Bridget Fonda spotted in rare LA outing 24 years after her final on-screen appearance
summary: Bridget Fonda was spotted out in Los Angeles 24 years after her last on-screen role, having previously told paparazzi she has no plans to return to acting.
story: The former actress was photographed Nov. 2, while out to lunch in Los Angeles.
Bridget Fonda stepped out for a rare public outing in Los Angeles, 24 years after she last appeared on-screen.
The 62-year-old actress was photographed while out to lunch on Monday, Nov. 2, keeping it casual in black sweatpants and a white tank top, paired with a yellow collared button-up shirt.
She accessorized the look with a black crossbody bag and sunglasses, and styled her hair in a ponytail.

As the granddaughter of Academy Award-winning actor, Henry Fonda, known for his roles in "The Grapes of Wrath," "12 Angry Men" and "On Golden Pond," Bridget made her film debut when she was five years old, appearing alongside her father, Peter Fonda, in the 1969 movie, "Easy Rider."
Bridget Fonda was photographed while out having lunch with a friend in Los Angeles. (The Image Direct)
'80S ICON KRISTY MCNICHOL MAKES RARE APPEARANCE 25 YEARS AFTER LEAVING HOLLYWOOD

Although she found big success as an actress, she slowed down in the late 1990s and into the 2000s. Her final movie role was in the 2001 TV movie, "After Amy," and her final time on-screen was in two episodes of the miniseries "Snow Queen," in 2002.
Bridget's final on-screen role was in two episodes of "Snow Queen" in 2002. (KMazur/WireImage)

title: Dustin Hoffman had a 'terrible experience' making Hollywood classic 'The Graduate'
summary: Dustin Hoffman reveals in a new essay that he felt "unworthy" and feared being fired every day while filming "The Graduate" with Mike Nichols.
story: The actor shared he didn't feel he was right for the part and felt tension with the film's director, Mike Nichols.
Dustin Hoffman is opening up about the "terrible experience" he had while filming "The Graduate," a film he said "exacerbated all my insecurities from the start."

In a recent essay written for The New Yorker, the 89-year-old actor reflected on his experience making the film, which earned him his first Academy Award nomination and a BAFTA Award win, noting he "felt immediately uncomfortable" and "unworthy" on set.

"Here I was, playing a starring role in a movie by Mike Nichols, who was the director of the moment, but I felt like I had no right to be there," he wrote. "It was a terrible experience making the movie that changed my life."

He went on to explain that a lot of his time on set was spent wondering if director, Nichols, "was angry at me," because he was either "doing something wrong" or had finally noticed what Hoffman and "everybody else already knew, that he had miscast the lead in his film."
Hoffman called working on "The Graduate" a "terrible experience." (Getty Images)
JOHN GOODMAN ADMITS HE FELT 'FRIGHTENED' AFTER THE SUDDEN FAME HE EXPERIENCED FROM 'ROSEANNE'

The "Rain Man" star felt he was wrong for the part from the start, admitting he "didn't even want to try out for the part," saying he thought "it was obvious" to him after reading the novel the film is based on "that I was all wrong for Benjamin."

"A track star and straight-A student, the head of the debate team—this was an affluent, all-American kid, whose surname was ‘Braddock,’" he said. "Why would you cast a person who looks as ethnic as I do to play the ultimate Wasp? It made absolutely no sense."
Hoffman recalled feeling like he was wrong for the part from the beginning. (Screen Archives/Getty Images)
Part of what made the experience so bad for Hoffman was his relationship with the director, who he said was "irritable with everyone," and was "frequently sour" on set.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

The director's attitude often led to Hoffman feel "that I was about to be fired," as the actor found himself "thinking, I have no f- - -ing idea what I'm doing," while filming some of the most well-known scenes in the movie.
Hoffman recalled the director's "frequently sour" mood while on set. (Michael Loccisano/Getty Images)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Hoffman also recalled feeling as if the director had a "certain sadism" that was directed mostly towards him.

"There was a scene in which Katharine Ross had to slap me, and he made us do twenty-seven takes. The scene has Benjamin run into Elaine’s room, soaking wet from the rain, to tell her that he’s had an affair with an older woman; within seconds, Elaine realizes the woman is her mother," he said. "Mike just kept telling Katharine to hit me, to hit me harder. Katharine worried she would hurt me, and I told her, ‘I’m O.K. Just don’t hit my ear.’ Unfortunately, she missed a few times. I was dizzy by the end of that day, and Mike didn’t even use the slap in the film."
Hoffman was slapped by his costar 27 times for a scene that ended up being cut. (Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images)
The next day, Hoffman was scheduled to film a scene underwater, which left him with "blood trickling out of my ear," which later turned out to be a punctured eardrum.

"The Graduate" went on to become one of Hoffman's most well-known films. The movie follows Hoffman's character, Benjamin, a recent college graduate who is struggling to find direction post graduation and is seduced by an older housewife and friend of his parents.

title: 'Blue Lagoon' star Christopher Atkins wanted to be a dad more than 'a drunk' as he nears 40 years sober

story: Christopher Atkins told Fox News Digital at the Chiller Theatre Expo why becoming a dad motivated him to get sober nearly 40 years ago and how his grandchildren keep him committed today.
Christopher Atkins says becoming a father gave him a reason to walk away from alcohol, and nearly four decades later, his grandchildren are giving him another reason to stay sober.

The former Hollywood heartthrob, who rose to fame opposite Brooke Shields in 1980's "The Blue Lagoon," opened up about the turning point that changed his life during an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital at the Chiller Theatre Expo in New Jersey.
"I guess the turning point for me was having children, so I wanted to be a dad more than I wanted to be a drunk," Atkins said.

Atkins previously spoke about how his drinking affected his Hollywood career, including an opportunity to star in the 1984 film "Footloose."

During an appearance at Fanboy Expo Knoxville earlier this year, the actor said he had been considered for the lead role that ultimately went to Kevin Bacon but was drinking heavily when he met with filmmakers.

Macklemore is claiming that Madison Square Garden and the Kia Forum are among venues who refused to host his Free Palestine tour.

On Friday, Macklemore, whose legal name is Ben Haggerty, uploaded a lengthy statement to Instagram, claiming it has been difficult for him to bring his Free Palestine tour to the United States. He claimed nine major venues across the U.S. turned him down.

Madison Square Garden, Prudential Center, Barclays Center, UBS Arena, Intuit Dome, Kia Forum, Crypto.com Arena, Chase Center and Climate Pledge Arena were among the venues that said no, according to Macklemore.
He emphasized that their decision came "once they found out these were my benefit shows for Palestine."

"Look at what just happened in Europe. Three sold-out arenas. Tens of thousands of people from different backgrounds, religions and walks of life standing together. More than forty artists and speakers putting their names and platforms behind Palestinian liberation. title: Defense attorney in Tupac Shakur murder trial found dead at 55: report
summary: Michael Sanft, the Las Vegas attorney who defended Duane Davis in the Tupac Shakur murder trial, was reportedly found dead days after filing an appeal in the case.
story: Jurors on Monday reached a verdict in the trial of Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis, who was charged in Tupac Shakur’s 1996 killing.

Michael Sanft, the Las Vegas defense attorney who represented Duane "Keffe D" Davis in the Tupac Shakur murder case, was found dead inside his home Friday morning, according to the Las Vegas Review-Journal.
He was 55.
The cause and manner of Sanft's death has not yet been determined. Police told the Las Vegas outlet the death did not appear suspicious.
Michael Sloan, a close friend who rode motorcycles with Sanft, according to the report, confirmed his death and remembered the attorney as a devoted friend.
DUANE 'KEFFE D' DAVIS FOUND GUILTY OF FIRST-DEGREE MURDER IN 1996 KILLING OF TUPAC SHAKUR

Michael Sanft, the defense attorney who represented Duane "Keffe D" Davis in the Tupac Shakur murder trial, has reportedly died at age 55, days after filing an appeal challenging his client's conviction. (David Becker/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)
"He was one of my best friends and one of the best human beings I knew," Sloan shared.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Clark County Coroner's Office and the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department for comment.
Tupac Shakur was shot in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas Sept. 7, 1996, and died six days later at age 25. (Raymond Boyd/Getty Images)
TUPAC SHAKUR MURDER TRIAL'S FIRST WEEK SEES HEATED TESTIMONY FROM RELUCTANT WITNESSES WITH OLD GANGLAND TIES
Sanft's death comes after a courtroom battle that ended with Davis, 63, becoming the first person convicted in Shakur's 1996 murder.
Duane "Keffe D" Davis was convicted of first-degree murder in the 1996 killing of rapper Tupac Shakur and sentenced to 40 years to life in prison. (John Locher/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)
A Nevada jury found Davis guilty of first-degree murder with the use of a deadly weapon in August. He was sentenced Oct. 13 to 40 years to life behind bars, according to The Associated Press.
The verdict marked a significant development in a case that has drawn international attention for nearly three decades.

Shakur was riding in a BMW with Death Row Records co-founder Marion "Suge" Knight near the Las Vegas Strip Sept. 7, 1996, when a gunman in a white Cadillac opened fire.
Knight survived with minor injuries. Shakur, one of hip-hop's biggest stars at the time, died six days later at age 25.
Defense attorney Michael Sanft cross-examines James McDonald during the murder trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis related to the 1996 killing of rapper Tupac Shakur. (John Locher/Pool via Reuters)
Prosecutors argued Davis orchestrated the killing after his nephew was involved in a fight with Shakur and Knight earlier that night.

During closing arguments, prosecutor Binu Palal told jurors Davis obtained a gun and "went hunting" for the two men. Prosecutors also pointed to Davis' own statements placing himself inside the Cadillac used in the shooting.
Sanft disputed the prosecution's case, telling jurors there was no evidence beyond Davis' statements placing his client in Las Vegas or inside the Cadillac.
Jurors deliberated for about three hours before finding Davis guilty.

The decision prompted an emotional scene in court, with Shakur's sister, Sekyiwa "Set" Shakur, crying as the verdict was read. Davis' son covered his face with one hand.
The jury consisted of 12 jurors and four alternates. The panel heard testimony over nine days from 24 prosecution witnesses and three defense witnesses.

title: Martha Stewart begs America for forgiveness after 'stupid' homeless Halloween costume sparks backlash
summary: Martha Stewart admits her homeless Halloween costume was "stupid" after her grandson warned her it was "tone-deaf" before the backlash began.
story: 'The Five' co-hosts discuss Martha Stewart's decision to delete a controversial Halloween photo showing her dressed as a homeless person and her apology.
Martha Stewart is asking Americans for forgiveness after her Halloween costume drew harsh criticism.
The lifestyle mogul, 85, admitted her decision to dress as a homeless person was "stupid," and revealed that her grandson had warned her about the outfit before the public criticism began.
"According to my grandson, I was tone-deaf," Stewart said while explaining how the controversial costume came together during an appearance Friday on the "Today" show.
MARTHA STEWART ADDRESSES BACKLASH AFTER DRESSING AS HOMELESS PERSON FOR HALLOWEEN
Martha Stewart's Halloween costume has sparked outrage online, with some describing the TV personality as "out of touch." (Getty Images; Martha Stewart/Instagram)
Stewart's Halloween costume featured ripped jeans, a distressed shirt and a cardboard sign that said, "I AM HUNGRY. HELP ME!!"
During a discussion about lessons learned on the morning show, she acknowledged she needed to be more mindful and "pay closer attention to social issues. Be aware."
The businesswoman said she cares deeply about the challenges facing Americans but acknowledged that her costume was a mishap.
"But I made a mistake. I mean, I was stupid. Yeah. What else can I say? What else can I say? I'm so sorry," Stewart said.
MARTHA STEWART GETS CANDID ABOUT PLASTIC SURGERY, DATING AS SHE TURNS 85
Martha Stewart asked for forgiveness after facing criticism for dressing as a homeless person for Halloween. (Katie Jones/WWD via Getty Images)

She also asked her fans and the public to forgive her, saying, "I hope that my followers and my fans and the rest of America forgives me for doing something that was not meant in any way to be a bad thing."
The longtime television personality said she put together the costume at the last minute after initially deciding not to dress up for Halloween.

A chocolate stain on her white sweater also helped inspire the last-minute costume, Stewart said. She joked that "Today" co-anchor Craig Melvin was responsible for the stain before clarifying that she was only kidding.
In her initial statement to Page Six, Stewart said the costume was not meant to mock people experiencing homelessness.

"I am distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people, which was never my intention," she said.

title: Meghan Markle's estrangement from father Thomas Markle: From royal wedding fallout to his arrest
summary: Thomas Markle Sr. was arrested Friday in Florida on child pornography charges. Meghan Markle and her father have been estranged for years.
story: Meghan Markle's estranged father, 82, was arrested in Florida and charged with possession of child sexual abuse images after an FBI investigation. (Video courtesy: The Sun)
Meghan Markle's father, Thomas Markle Sr., has spent years in the public eye after his highly publicized falling-out with the Duchess of Sussex ahead of her 2018 royal wedding.
Now, the former Hollywood lighting director is facing an entirely separate legal battle after being arrested and charged with possession of child sexual abuse material.
Markle Sr. was arrested in Florida after FBI agents raided his nursing home.

Meghan Markle’s relationship with her father, Thomas Markle Sr., deteriorated publicly shortly before her 2018 wedding to Prince Harry. (Getty Images)

A number of armed federal agents descended on Markle Sr.’s care center around 9 a.m. Friday, taking the wheelchair-bound father of the Duchess of Sussex into custody. Agents handcuffed Markle Sr. before wheeling him to an ambulance, which transported him to court.
WATCH: THOMAS MARKLE HANDCUFFED IN FBI CHILD PORNOGRAPHY ARREST
Here's a look at the key moments in the Markle family's public history, from Meghan and her father's estrangement to the criminal investigation that led to Thomas' arrest.
May 2018: Meghan Markle begins to distance herself from Thomas Markle Sr.

Meghan's relationship with her father deteriorated publicly in May 2018, as she was about to marry Prince Harry. Just days before the royal wedding, he became embroiled in a controversy involving staged paparazzi photographs.
Markle Sr. initially denied staging the paparazzi photographs and later said he had suffered a heart attack and needed medical treatment, preventing him from traveling to England for the ceremony.

In August 2018, Meghan wrote her father a deeply personal letter asking him to stop discussing their relationship with the media. The following year, Britain's Mail on Sunday published portions of the handwritten letter after Markle Sr. shared it with the newspaper. Meghan subsequently sued for misuse of private information and copyright infringement.
Their estrangement continued in the years that followed, with Markle Sr. publicly expressing disappointment over their lack of contact.

Thomas Markle Sr. did not attend the royal wedding after saying he had a heart attack and needed medical treatment. (News Licensing/Mega Agency)

On Oct. 29, 2026, the Metropolitan Police confirmed that they had referred their handling of the letter to the Independent Office for Police Conduct, the U.K.'s police watchdog.

Meghan's father pleaded to meet his grandchildren, Archie and Lilibet, and said he was "very concerned" that he wouldn't live long enough to meet them.

"We’re at a point where, I think both of us, we should grow up, talk, make up for the sake of the children," the former Hollywood lighting director said during an appearance on "Good Morning Britain." "This is ridiculous. Almost four years. It’s crazy.

"My message for the kids is that they have two loving families," he said at the time. "I think it’s important for them to know that they have two families, and eventually they’re going to grow up, and they’re going to want to know more about them."
PRINCE HARRY MAKING 'BIG MISTAKE' THAT COULD DESTROY CHANCE OF ROYAL RECONCILIATION: EXPERT

December 2025: Thomas Markle Sr. pleads for reconciliation with Meghan Markle after 'life-or-death' leg surgery
Markle Sr. underwent a "life-or-death" leg amputation in 2025 and spoke to the Daily Mail about wanting to reconcile with Meghan.

"I've always said I am open to reconciling with my daughter," he told the outlet. "I have never stopped loving her. I don't want to die estranged from Meghan. I want to meet my grandkids. It might be nice to meet her husband too."
A spokesperson confirmed to People that the Duchess of Sussex had contacted her father.
"I can confirm she has reached out to her father," the spokesperson said. Meghan's representative did not share any further details about her contact with her father.

Thomas Markle Jr. told the Daily Mail his father's leg was amputated Dec. 3 in the Philippines, where the pair had been living since the beginning of 2025. According to Thomas Jr., a blood clot in his father's thigh cut off circulation to his leg, leading to the surgery.
The Metropolitan Police said it received a 2019 letter containing claims about alleged offenses outside the U.K. The force said it is reviewing how it handled the matter. (News Licensing/MEGA)

title: Men and women who smoke marijuana may experience different effects, study suggests
summary: UCLA researchers found occasional male cannabis users reported stronger effects like anxiety and elevated heart rate than women with similar THC levels.
story: Family physician Dr. Jessica Gray discusses the rising trend of daily marijuana use in America. She warns against the common misconception that cannabis is naturally safe and highlights the lack of evidence supporting its mental health benefits.
Men who use cannabis occasionally may feel stronger effects from the drug than women with similar use habits, new research suggests.

The UCLA Health study, published in the journal Neuropsychopharmacology, included 44 healthy adults between the ages of 21 and 55, evenly split between men and women. Researchers divided participants based on whether they used cannabis frequently or occasionally.
Each participant took part in three separate sessions: smoking cannabis with no THC, a lower amount of THC or a higher amount. They did not know which one they were receiving at the time.
MARIJUANA USERS MAY FACE HIDDEN DRIVING DANGER THAT STANDARD TESTS CAN MISS
Among those who used cannabis occasionally, men reported feeling more high, sedated and impaired than women with similar use habits, according to the study.
The men also reported more unpleasant effects, including anxiety, and their heart rate rose significantly after using active cannabis.
Men who use cannabis occasionally may feel stronger effects from the drug than women with similar use habits, new research suggests. (iStock)
Blood THC levels alone did not appear to explain the difference.
Men and women who used cannabis occasionally had similar peak THC levels, even though the men reported stronger effects, researchers found.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER
The pattern was different among people who used cannabis more often. Men and women in the frequent-use group generally responded similarly to active cannabis.
Frequent users were also more likely than occasional users to say they liked the effects, wanted to use cannabis again and chose to take more during the study, regardless of gender.
Men who smoke cannabis occasionally may experience greater intoxication, sedation and impairment than women who use the drug at similar frequencies. (iStock)
The findings challenge some previous research suggesting women may be more sensitive to the effects of cannabis.

"Much of what we thought we knew about sex differences in cannabis effects came from animal research and from human studies that pooled data from different trials," Dr. Ziva Cooper, the study's principal investigator and director of the UCLA Center for Cannabis and Cannabinoids, said in a press release.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES
"When we designed a study to look at sex and frequency of use at the same time, and controlled for hormones, the picture changed," she added.
The researchers controlled for menstrual cycle timing among the women in the study, who were not using hormonal birth control.
The findings suggest that a person's history of cannabis use may be an important factor in determining how strongly the drug affects them. (iStock)
The findings suggest that a person's cannabis habits may be important when considering how men and women respond to the drug.

"Sex and cannabis use history can both shape how someone experiences the effects of cannabis," lead author Dr. Stephanie Lake, a researcher at the UCLA Center for Cannabis and Cannabinoids, said in the release.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
"Studying both together is key to understanding who is most at risk of higher-risk, unpleasant or beneficial experiences from cannabis."
There were several limitations to the findings, the researchers acknowledged.
Researchers noted that cannabis products sold today commonly contain THC concentrations of 20% or higher, exceeding the strengths tested in the study. (iStock)
The study was small, with just 44 participants, and several of the findings involving occasional male users came from exploratory analyses, meaning they need to be confirmed in larger studies.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The cannabis used in the experiment contained 4% or 10% THC, which researchers noted is weaker than many cannabis products sold today, where THC levels are commonly 20% or higher.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Researchers said larger studies are needed to better understand whether men and women develop tolerance to cannabis differently and how those differences could affect the risk of cannabis use disorder.
Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.

title: 6-minute daily habit could help Ozempic users preserve muscle, expert says
summary: Gary Brecka says just six minutes of daily resistance training can help protect lean body mass during Ozempic and Wegovy weight loss journeys.
story: Gary Brecka, a biologist and longevity expert in Miami, Florida, shared with Fox News Digital his simple strategy for helping people preserve muscle — starting with just six minutes of exercise a day.
As more Americans turn to popular GLP-1 medications such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Zepbound to lose weight or manage diabetes, there is a growing focus on protecting muscle as pounds are shed.
The concern comes as 11% of U.S. adults report taking these drugs for weight loss, up from 3% in 2024, according to Gallup.
Lean mass, which includes muscle and other tissues, accounts for roughly a quarter to a third of the weight lost with these obesity treatments, research suggests.
4 SIMPLE HABITS CAN HELP SLOW MUSCLE LOSS AS YOU AGE, FITNESS EXPERT SAYS

Gary Brecka, a biologist and longevity expert in Miami, Florida, shared with Fox News Digital his simple strategy for helping people preserve muscle — starting with just six minutes of exercise a day.

"GLP-1s can be life-saving for people, especially for people who are morbidly obese or have type 2 diabetes, but they can also be fascinating shifts in someone's trajectory of their wellness journey," he said.
Lean mass, which includes muscle and other tissues, accounts for roughly a quarter to a third of the weight lost with GLP-1 medications. (iStock)
"What's critically important for people who embark on a GLP-1 journey is to make sure that they are mitigating the lean body-mass loss."
Brecka emphasized that weight loss is not exclusively fat loss.
OZEMPIC USERS MAY BE MAKING A MAJOR WEIGHT-LOSS MISTAKE, NEW STUDY SUGGESTS

"When most people say, ‘I want to lose weight,’ what they're really saying is, ‘I want to lose fat,’" he said. "But with GLP-1s, you have a double-edged sword. About 20% to 40% of the weight that you lose is what we call lean body mass."

Lean body mass includes not only muscle, but also water, organs, blood and connective tissues, such as tendons and ligaments. Brecka emphasized that preserving lean tissue should be a priority during treatment.
"You don't have to lift like a bodybuilder to mitigate lean body mass loss."
Maintaining strength also helps people remain independent as they age, supporting everyday activities such as bathing, dressing and walking.
"The more that we can maintain control and dominion over those, the more independent we can be," Brecka said.
WEEKLY WEIGHTLIFTING SWEET SPOT MAY BE LINKED TO LONGER LIFE, STUDY FINDS
Strength in minutes
Challenging the body through exercise encourages it to adapt and grow stronger, Brecka said.
"But when it comes to a GLP-1 journey, you've got to give up a little bit of that comfort to reach your goals," he said.
Challenging the body through exercise encourages it to adapt and grow stronger, the expert said. (iStock)
Brecka recommends starting with six minutes of resistance exercise each day.

"People think of weight-training or resistance training as something they've got to dedicate 60 to 90 minutes to every day, and therefore they think they don't have enough time in their day," he said.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
It’s also important to pair the strength training with adequate protein to help preserve muscle during weight loss.
Protein provides amino acids that help the body build and maintain muscle and other tissues, including tendons, ligaments and cartilage, Brecka said.
‘Snacking’ on exercise
Busy people who don’t have time for lengthy gym sessions can fit resistance training into their day by "snacking" on exercise, the longevity expert said.
Brecka suggested simple exercises such as holding a plank with the knees on the floor, progressing to a full plank as strength allows, or doing body-weight squats and abdominal crunches.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

He also recommended resistance exercises using dumbbells or barbells, preferably moving through a full range of motion. One example is a goblet squat, which involves holding a dumbbell near the chest while squatting and standing.

"You don't have to lift like a bodybuilder to mitigate lean body mass loss," he said. "All you have to do is provide resistance for these tissues so that your body doesn't begin to reabsorb them while you're on this GLP-1 journey."
Busy people who don’t have time for lengthy gym sessions can fit resistance training into their day by "snacking" on exercise, the longevity expert said. (iStock)

In terms of frequency, Brecka said exercise should be "non-negotiable" as a daily practice. He recommends a minimum of three days of resistance training and a minimum of three days of cardiovascular training.

"Cardiovascular training can be as simple as walking outside, taking your dog for a 20-minute walk," he said, adding that a weighted vest can make the same walk more challenging by increasing the load the body carries.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"If you're going to an airport, skip the moving walkway, skip the escalator, just take the steps," Brecka suggested. "There are simple things that you can do every single day … that have a dramatic impact on your body's ability to rebuild these tissues."
"These small choices throughout our lifetime are what build resilience for the decades ahead."
Prioritizing protein
Protein does more than just support muscle, according to Brecka.

Whether protein comes from chicken, beef or plant-based foods, the body breaks it down into amino acids that help build and repair muscle and other tissues, including tendons, ligaments and cartilage.
The body breaks down protein from foods such as chicken, beef and plants into amino acids, which help build and repair muscle and other tissues, including tendons, ligaments and cartilage. (iStock)
"Protein is important for so many more things than just muscle and the physical things that we see on the outside," Brecka said. "It's also responsible for building these lean body mass structures."
Current federal dietary guidelines recommend 1.2 to 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight daily.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A joint advisory on GLP-1 treatment discusses the same range during active weight loss, while emphasizing that targets should be tailored to the individual.

Brecka also urged patients to pay attention to declining energy or exercise performance, such as finding a previously easy flight of stairs suddenly difficult, and discuss those changes with a doctor.

title: Forget prunes: Popular green fruit shows promise for constipation relief
summary: A review of 33 studies links eating two green kiwis daily for four weeks to more regular bowel movements in people with constipation or IBS-C.
story: Christopher Gardner, PhD, a nutrition scientist at Stanford University, says increasing fiber is crucial in a healthy diet and recommends eating more fruits, vegetables and minimally processed foods rather than eliminating an entire food group.
Eating two green kiwis a day could help people struggling with constipation, a new review suggests.
The research, published in the journal Food, Nutrition and Health, looked at 33 previous studies and reports on kiwifruit and digestive health.

Eating two fresh green kiwis a day for about four weeks was linked to more regular bowel movements, less straining and better digestive comfort in people with constipation or irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C).
COMMON KITCHEN STAPLE MAY HELP RELIEVE MILD CONSTIPATION, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

In one international trial included in the review, people with constipation had about 1.5 more complete bowel movements per week, while those with IBS-C had about 1.7 more per week. Both groups also reported improved digestive comfort.
The new review suggests there may be several reasons kiwi helps with constipation.
Eating two green kiwis a day could help people struggling with constipation, a new review suggests. (iStock)

Its fiber can add bulk and hold water in stool, while the fruit's natural water and sorbitol may help make stool easier to pass. Researchers said the benefit likely comes from several parts of the whole fruit working together rather than one component alone.
Kiwi was not necessarily more effective than other constipation treatments.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

One U.S. trial included in the review found that green kiwi, psyllium fiber and prunes all helped improve chronic constipation. Kiwi was associated with fewer side effects and was well-tolerated by many participants.
The evidence is strongest for fresh green kiwi, the researchers noted. There is less research on gold kiwi, powders and extracts, so those forms should not be assumed to have the same effect.
Researchers found that consuming two green kiwis daily for about four weeks was linked to more regular bowel movements and less straining. (iStock)

Jason Heiselman, a New York-based certified nutritionist and professional chef at Hungryroot in New York City, previously told Fox News Digital that kiwi is an easy fruit to work into a person's diet.
"It feels like a no-brainer to include a few slices with any meal," said Heiselman, who was not involved in the new review.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Kiwi contains fiber along with a natural enzyme called actinidin, which can help with digestion, the nutritionist noted.
"Pairing kiwi with some good fat sources, like seeds, nuts or full-fat dairy, allows your body to absorb more nutrients," he said.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
For people who do not want to eat kiwi on its own, the fruit can also work in savory meals, according to Heiselman. "Raw kiwi slices often make their way to my dinner table," he said.
Heiselman said he pairs the fruit with salty cheeses, toasted pistachios and shaved red onion, and has also used kiwi as the base for chutneys and relishes.
Although green kiwi showed promise for constipation relief, researchers said it was not necessarily more effective than other dietary options. (iStock)
There were some limitations to the findings.

The paper reviewed previous research rather than conducting a new clinical trial, and the studies differed in the people involved, the types and amounts of kiwi consumed, and the results researchers measured.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Most of the research also looked at relatively short periods of time, so more studies are needed to determine whether the benefits continue long-term.
Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.

title: Pro-life pregnancy center expands mission to help patients embrace their God-given gender
summary: By listening to the Holy Spirit, Heidi Matzke, executive director of the Alternatives Pregnancy Center, said her clinic helps women embrace the gender they were given by God.
story: A mother shares her experience with pro-life crisis pregnancy centers, Life First in Manassas, Virginia, opened its doors to Fox News Digital to discuss how it helps pregnant women in crisis.
Helping a transgender man detransition to being a woman again is not something the pro-life, gospel-led Alternatives Pregnancy Center even notes on its website.

But because it is a full-service women's health clinic with doctors who specialize in hormone therapy, it's simply something they do in order to give women the care they need to fully embrace their God-given gender.
It is all based on listening to the Holy Spirit, said executive director Heidi Matzke.
STUDY REVEALS UNEXPECTED HEALTH BENEFITS AFTER 5 MINUTES OF PRAYER

Based in Sacramento, California, Alternatives is one of hundreds of like-minded pregnancy help centers across the country. These venues may have different names, but they all work to help women with unplanned pregnancies.
Still, years ago when Matzke took over, she knew she needed help — heavenly help.
A health center located in Sacramento, California, not only helps women with unplanned pregnancies — it is also a full-service women's health clinic propelled by faith (not pictured). (iStock)

Matzke told Fox News, "When God called me into this ministry... I felt the Holy Spirit impress upon my heart back then, 'Heidi, you're right. You have no idea what you're doing, and that's why you'd better be face-down before me every single day. You better be fasting and praying.'"
She did fast. And she prayed and listened, she said.
The result today is a pregnancy help center that is also a full-service health clinic for women.
New challenges
It wasn't long before another challenge came Matzke's way, involving listening to God.
She asked the Holy Spirit to direct her very short talk at a church soon after launching the full-service clinic. The pastor gave her just two minutes.
By listening to the Holy Spirit, Heidi Matzke became the angel in Jessica Rose's life.
Matzke heard the Holy Spirit say to talk only about the women's health services the center offered and nothing else — not even the unplanned pregnancy help.

Then, between services, a man dressed as a woman came to her in the pews.
It wasn't long before another challenge arrived that involved listening closely to God. (boonchai wedmakawand via Getty Images)

He said to her, "What you don't know about me is that I'm biologically female, and I encountered Christ. The Holy Spirit has done work in my heart, and I am now trying to detransition. But my current doctors have basically abandoned me and I have nowhere to go."

The woman had been "sobbing uncontrollably" — and praying God would help her with her serious medical issues. (iStock)

title: Struggling with depression? Psychiatrist says 6 habits may be making it worse
summary: Dr. Daniel Amen reveals the everyday habits that worsen depression, from alcohol use and isolation to processed foods and unchecked negative thoughts.
story: Dr. Daniel Amen, founder of Amen Clinics, identifies six behaviors people should avoid when experiencing depression, including drinking alcohol, withdrawing from others and consuming highly processed foods.

Depression rates among Americans ages 12 and older rose nearly 60% over a decade, increasing from 8.2% in 2013–2014 to 13.1% in 2021–2023, according to a recent report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
Finding the right treatment for depression can take time, and antidepressants usually take four to eight weeks to work, per the National Institute of Mental Health.

For those struggling with the condition, clinical psychiatrist Dr. Daniel Amen – founder of Amen Clinics in California – says avoiding the following habits may help to manage symptoms and support mental health.
IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE
No. 1: Drinking alcohol
Alcohol may offer temporary relief from depression symptoms, but as its effects wear off, mood can worsen.
Dr. Daniel Amen (right) is the founder of brain scan company Amen Clinics in California. (Katie Levine; iStock)
As the brain adjusts to alcohol’s relaxing effects, it can leave people feeling more anxious and restless after the buzz fades, making them feel "worse than before," Amen warned.
Drinking can also disrupt sleep, adding to next-day fatigue, according to the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism.
No. 2: Staying in bed
It might be tempting to linger in bed when you wake up, but Amen encouraged people with depression to get up and start their day.

"When people are depressed, they tend to have pretty low activity, especially in the front part of their brain, but burying yourself under the covers just makes things worse," he said. "Get up, get out."
SCIENTISTS REVEAL SURPRISINGLY EASY EXERCISE THAT MAY BOOST YOUR MOOD IN JUST 10 MINUTES
Amen's advice aligns with a broader approach called behavioral activation, a type of therapy that helps people gradually return to meaningful activities rather than withdraw from them.
Behavioral activation has been shown to be beneficial for treating depression, according to a 2020 Cochrane review of 53 studies involving 5,495 adults.
"Burying yourself under the covers just makes things worse," Amen said in reference to depression. (iStock)
No. 3: Believing your negative thoughts
A negative mindset can make it easier to believe things that aren’t true — or, as Amen puts it, every "stupid" thought. He refers to these as "ANTs," or automatic negative thoughts.
"The thoughts that come into your mind automatically and ruin your day – they drive depression," he said.
"Burying yourself under the covers just makes things worse … get up, get out."
When feeling strong emotions – such as sadness, anger, anxiety or just lack of control – Amen recommends writing down what you’re thinking and then asking yourself if it’s true.
"My favorite part – and there's a whole method to this – is flipping the thought and actually meditating on the opposite of the thought you have," he said. "So, taking each thought captive."
No. 4: Isolating yourself
Depression can lead people to withdraw from others, but social isolation may worsen symptoms, Amen said.
"The more isolated you get, the louder the ANT chorus gets, and it makes [depression] worse," he cautioned.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

A 2025 study published in General Hospital Psychiatry tracked more than 339,000 U.K. adults for roughly 12 years. Loneliness was associated with a 77% higher risk of developing depression, while social isolation was linked to a 14% higher risk.
No. 5: Eating highly processed foods
Eating more ultraprocessed foods, including many fast-food items, has been linked to a higher risk of depression, Amen said, although research has not established cause and effect.
"There's actually a lot of consensus now among psychiatrists that inflammation drives certain types of depression," the doctor told Fox News Digital.
A negative mindset can make it easier to believe things that aren’t true — which Amen refers to these as "ANTs," or automatic negative thoughts. (iStock)
A 2025 review in the American Journal of Psychiatry supports inflammation’s role in some cases, but notes that elevated inflammatory markers occurred in only a subset of people with depression.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Amen recommends adhering to an anti-inflammatory diet emphasizing "vegetables, healthy protein and healthy fats."

A 2024 review of five randomized trials involving 1,507 adults found that Mediterranean-style diets reduced depressive symptoms compared with control groups, although results varied considerably among studies.
No. 6: Taking medication without a proper assessment
Depression treatment is individualized, so not every medication is right for everyone — and not every patient requires medication.
Amen emphasized the importance of receiving a thorough assessment prior to receiving antidepressants, which he said can be "lifesaving."
Some supplements, like omega-3 and saffron, have been found to be more effective than antidepressants in recent research. (iStock)

For milder depression, psychotherapy is often the first approach. People with moderate or severe depression are usually prescribed medication as part of their initial treatment plan, according to the National Institute of Mental Health.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

For those who have done "all the right things" but still struggle, Amen encouraged seeking further medical evaluation. Depending on symptoms and medical history, a clinician may order blood tests to check for conditions such as anemia or thyroid disease that could contribute to symptoms.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The doctor also recommended considering approaches beyond medication, such as exercise — or, as Amen suggested, "walking like you're late" — which has been proven in studies to perform better than some depression medications.
Some supplements, like omega-3 and saffron, have been found to be more effective than antidepressants in recent research.
Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Simple bedtime change may help some individuals lose weight, study finds
summary: An NYU clinical trial found that moving bedtime just one hour earlier led to weight loss in prediabetes patients, even without longer sleep.
story: Metabolic health expert Jim LaValle explains how chronic stress, inadequate sleep and everyday dietary choices can affect blood sugar regulation and contribute to insulin resistance.
Falling asleep earlier was linked to greater weight loss in adults with prediabetes, according to new research.

An analysis of data from a randomized trial led by the NYU Rory Meyers College of Nursing found that each hour earlier participants fell asleep was associated with roughly 1. 3 pounds of weight loss over eight weeks, although the finding does not prove that moving bedtime earlier causes weight loss.

"When we fall asleep — not just how much we sleep — seems to be an important and overlooked factor for weight loss and metabolic health," Susan Kohl Malone, an assistant professor at the nursing college and the study's lead author, said in a press release.
POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY PREVENT PREDIABETES FROM TURNING INTO DIABETES

The investigation, published in the journal Nursing Research, evaluated 196 adults diagnosed with prediabetes who routinely logged fewer than 6.5 hours of sleep nightly. Half the group took part in an eight-week lifestyle education course on diet, exercise and stress.
Going to bed earlier was linked to weight loss in adults with prediabetes, independent of the total number of hours they spent asleep. (iStock)
The other half received the same training alongside behavioral coaching meant to get them to go to bed earlier in gradual phases.
DIETITIAN REVEALS SIMPLE EATING STRATEGY FOR BETTER SLEEP — AND ONE HABIT TO AVOID
Researchers tracked participants’ blood sugar, sleep and activity using sensors, sleep logs and wrist-worn monitors.

Neither group showed significant improvements in blood sugar. Both groups lost weight, but those receiving sleep coaching did not lose significantly more than those receiving lifestyle education alone.
Participants who received sleep coaching did report better sleep quality and less daytime drowsiness, and they gradually began going to bed earlier. (iStock)
"While we expected that extending sleep would improve glucose levels and weight loss in adults with prediabetes who sleep for shorter periods, this wasn't the case in our study," Malone said.
Participants who received sleep coaching did report better sleep quality and less daytime drowsiness, and they gradually began going to bed earlier.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
In a separate analysis across both groups, participants who shifted their sleep earlier tended to lose more weight.

The researchers suggested the body’s internal clock may help explain the findings. Staying up late can increase exposure to artificial light, which may activate the body’s stress response and affect hormones that regulate hunger.
A statistical projection from the study found that every 60 minutes earlier a participant fell asleep was associated with roughly 1.3 pounds of weight loss across eight weeks. (iStock)
Remaining awake late also coincides with the hours when human insulin sensitivity is at its lowest.
"In contrast, falling asleep earlier may limit late-night eating and better align food intake with the body's optimal metabolic window," Malone noted.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
The trial ran for only eight weeks, which means it's unclear whether participants could maintain earlier bedtimes or sustain weight loss over the long term.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
While participants wore wrist monitors, key sleep metrics like rest quality and daytime drowsiness relied heavily on self-reported logs.
Researchers noted that staying awake late elevates hunger hormones like ghrelin and increases the likelihood of late-night eating when the body's insulin sensitivity is at its lowest. (iStock)
The findings also show an association across the study group rather than proven cause and effect.
Participants receiving sleep coaching fell asleep about 12 minutes earlier on average, according to Malone, which produced no measurable improvement in blood sugar levels.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The study received funding from the National Institute of Nursing Research, a division of the National Institutes of Health, and was conducted in collaboration with researchers from the University of Delaware.
