title: Trump says deportations were ‘too tough’ and hurt him in midterms
summary: The president said in an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes” that he would like to work out a deal with Democrats on immigration.
story: President Donald Trump conceded that his immigration policies were “too tough,” saying in an interview on CBS’ “60 Minutes” that aired Sunday that mass deportations hurt him during the midterm elections.
Trump said his policies had been overly harsh in removing undocumented immigrants who hadn’t committed crimes.

“I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally,” Trump said in the interview, which was recorded Friday.

He added that “a large group of people” think immigrants who are “good people, working in a landscaping company or working in a hotel or doing something ... and, in some cases, paying taxes,” should be “allowed to stay.”

Trump pointed to immigration as one of the areas in which he wanted to work with Democrats, saying yes when he was asked whether a deal could look like the creation of legal status for undocumented workers.

He said, however, that people “on the sort of pretty far right ... would like everybody taken out,” saying some of them were in his administration. Trump on Friday promoted Stephen Miller, who conceived of the mass deportation policy enacted since Trump returned to office, to White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles.
Trump also blamed “bad messaging” for Republicans’ crushing midterm losses last week and downplayed the Iran war’s impact on economic woes.

“I think it was bad messaging, maybe by me, but I would talk about it all the time,” Trump said, adding that the media did not cover “positive news for me. So I have to do it myself. I have to get it out there.”
Pressed by CBS News’ Ross Douthat about what the “bad message” was, Trump said, “We couldn’t get the word across.”

The White House has mostly been without a press secretary since late August, after Karoline Leavitt left the administration. Katie Zacharia briefly replaced Leavitt, but she left after just five days.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Trump also commented on his business dealings in the interview when Douthat asked about his net worth’s having increased by nearly $3 billion since he returned to office, prompting him to initially say, “So did everyone’s.”

Trump’s net worth is $7 billion, according to Forbes. It reported that the amount went up by $2.7 billion since he was elected in 2024 for a second term. Trump’s financial disclosure forms show he has made $1.4 billion in cryptocurrency earnings.

“I devote almost no time to my net worth. I don’t care. I have a lot of money, and far more than I ever thought I’d have. And I guess it’s gone up. I don’t even know,” Trump said. He added that one of his sons “watches over money,” adding that the two do not discuss finances.

Trump’s sons founded a cryptocurrency company, World Liberty Financial, two years ago. Trump himself is a co-owner, and investors include Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a member of the Abu Dhabi royal family and national security adviser for the United Arab Emirates.

“I think if I told you that story and it was about the Biden family, if I said Joe Biden is the part-owner of a company and it has all of these investments from the Middle East, you would say, ‘That sounds corrupt,’ right?” Douthat said, asking Trump how his stake in the company is different.
“Because I know nothing about it,” Trump answered, adding that he did not know when he was pressed about whether foreign investors in the company believe they are buying influence.

title: The ‘slam dunk’ that wasn’t: Promising cholesterol drug fails to prevent heart attacks or stroke
summary: An experimental drug that held great promise in driving down a dangerous form of cholesterol didn’t show any measurable impact on heart attack or stroke in a clinical trial.
story: An experimental drug that held great promise in driving down a dangerous form of cholesterol didn’t show any measurable impact on heart attack or stroke in a clinical trial. The failure of the Novartis drug pelacarsen to help people who have high levels of lipoprotein(a) stunned researchers, who called it a massive blow to preventive cardiology.

Results of the clinical trial of pelacarsen, an injection, presented Saturday at a meeting of the American Heart Association, found there were zero decreases in stroke, heart attack, cardiovascular deaths or the number of procedures to open blocked arteries or restore blood flow to the heart.

“I really thought that this was going to be a slam dunk,” said Dr. Amanda Doran, an assistant professor of medicine in the division of cardiovascular medicine at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Vanderbilt was one of nearly 800 sites involved in the clinical trial, called Horizon. “We were pretty invested, so it obviously hurts.”

Pelacarsen targets a stealthy and particularly lethal form of cholesterol called lipoprotein(a), or Lp(a). Much like low-density lipoprotein — LDL, or the “bad” cholesterol — Lp(a) causes plaque to build up in arteries. But it also helps form blood clots, and unlike LDL, it is entirely genetic.
About 1 in 5 Americans have high Lp(a), according to the American Heart Association. Most don’t realize they’re at risk.
Because people are born with those high levels, diet and exercise have no effect. That’s why heart experts have been so keen to find a drug that would handle the problem.
The Horizon trial included 8,322 people with high Lp(a) levels and who’d already had a heart attack, stroke or other heart problem within 10 years of starting the trial.
The drug did reduce Lp(a) significantly, by 78%, compared with a placebo drug that cut levels by 13%.
But that huge reduction ultimately meant nothing in terms of cardiovascular health.
Dr. Steven Nissen, the chief academic officer of the Heart, Vascular & Thoracic Institute at the Cleveland Clinic, led the trial. He said the dismal results took him by “extreme surprise.”

“Everybody, me included, believed that lowering levels of lipoprotein(a) substantially would reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events,” he said. “There is simply no evidence here that people that got more reduction did better.”

The findings, also published Saturday in the New England Journal of Medicine, confounded Nissen and other cardiologists who’ve long known that controlling other markers of heart health — LDL and blood pressure, for example — provides clear benefits.

“I have not seen a more shockingly neutral trial in a while,” said Dr. Karol Watson, co-director of the UCLA Program in Preventive Cardiology and a professor at UCLA’s David Geffen School of Medicine. Watson was not involved with the research.

There are several theories as to why the drug didn’t work as anticipated. It’s possible, Watson said, that the therapy was given too late in life to make a difference. The average age of Horizon’s study participants was 60, and they were followed for an average of five years.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“Remember that Lp(a) is a genetic disorder, so from the time a baby’s conceived, their Lp(a) is high. If we just swooped in in the last five years, maybe that’s too late,” Watson said.

Study participants were also treated aggressively in other ways to drive down their LDL cholesterol and get blood pressure readings into a healthy range. Participants may have also been taking aspirin because of a history of heart attack or stroke, which could have lessened Lp(a)’s clotting risk.
“How much of the Lp(a)-associated risk was remaining? We just don’t know,” Watson said.
Does Lp(a) still matter as a marker of heart health?

Doctors have only recently begun screening for it. Earlier this year, the American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association released guidelines that every adult should have their Lp(a) levels measured. It’s a blood test that’s done once because levels are fixed and don’t change over time.
Experts stress that Lp(a) remains an important and valuable indicator of heart disease risk, even though the Horizon study failed to show any health benefit to driving down Lp(a) levels.

“None of that invalidates Lp(a) as a robust marker of cardiovascular disease risk,” said Dr. John Wilkins, a cardiologist at Northwestern Medicine and a professor in the division of cardiology at Northwestern University’s Feinberg School of Medicine. Wilkins was also one of the authors of the Lp(a) guidelines.

“It’s still worth testing for Lp(a) because it can help identify individuals with a higher probability of an event, and we do have other interventions that can help reduce their risk,” Wilkins said. “It’s just that at present, at least with this particular drug in this particular group of patients, we did not see benefit. That doesn’t mean that we might not find something or some way to lower Lp(a) that reduces risk. We just need more science to figure that out.”

UCLA’s Watson and Vanderbilt’s Doran agreed. “We have really good data to show that Lp(a) levels are predictive of disease,” Doran said. “People who have high Lp(a) need to be aware of that in order to pursue aggressive prevention strategies.”
What’s next in treating Lp(a)?
No further study of pelacarsen is planned, Nissen said, but similar drugs are in the pipeline: Eli Lilly’s lepodisiran, Amgen’s olpasiran and Silence Therapeutics’ zerlasiran.

All are injections that work by blocking the liver’s ability to produce Lp(a), but use different approaches. Pelacarsen is what’s known as an antisense oligonucleotide. The others use a technology called small interfering RNA, or siRNA, and may have fewer side effects, such as injection site reactions, Nissen said, than pelacarsen.
Like pelacarsen, all reduce Lp(a). Clinical trials to show whether they have any real-world heart health effects are ongoing.
Eli Lilly is also studying an oral drug called muvalaplin, and CRISPR gene-editing technology designed to permanently switch off the gene that produces Lp(a) is in early development.
“I’m still so hopeful,” Doran said. “We’re going to get it in the end.”

title: Democratic lawmakers seek to restore deportation protections to Afghans in the U.S.
summary: A pair of House Democrats will try to bypass Republican leaders and force a vote to restore Temporary Protected Status to Afghan nationals in the United States by introducing a discharge petition when Congress returns Monday night.
story: A pair of House Democrats will try to bypass Republican leaders and force a vote to restore Temporary Protected Status to Afghan nationals in the United States by introducing a discharge petition when Congress returns Monday night.

Rep. Jason Crow, D-Colo., and Rep. Sam Liccardo, D-Calif., will file the petition, which would require signatures from 218 members to bring forth legislation to grant Afghans protection from deportation until mid-2029.

TPS, created by Congress in 1990, is a Department of Homeland Security program that allows migrants to live and work in the U.S. for up to 18 months if their home countries have been designated as unsafe. The time period can be extended.
President Donald Trump’s administration terminated the status for Afghanistan in May 2025, a designation that former President Joe Biden’s administration had granted in 2022.

“This administration is returning TPS to its original temporary intent,”  then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said at the time. She added that “Afghanistan has had an improved security situation, and its stabilizing economy no longer prevent them from returning to their home country.”
While the Trump administration recently planned to deport dozens of Afghan immigrants and asylum-seekers to Pakistan, a federal judge last week temporarily blocked that move.

Crow and Liccardo would need all current House Democrats and a handful of Republicans to sign on to their discharge petition to reach the necessary 218 signatures. The pair already introduced a special rule on Oct. 1, allowing them to start collecting signatures as soon as they submit the petition on Monday.

“Our Afghan partners put their lives on the line to help protect American servicemembers like me,” Crow, who served as a paratrooper and an Army Ranger in Iraq and Afghanistan, said in a statement. “I’m working to force a vote that will protect Afghans already in the United States because I won’t let our nation leave these brave Afghans behind.”

If Crow and Liccardo are successful in reaching the 218-signature threshold, GOP leaders would be forced to bring forward the Afghanistan TPS Act for a floor vote. That bill, which the pair introduced in July, would grant TPS to Afghans until July 2029. The legislation would need a majority vote on the House floor to pass.

The bill already has four Republican co-sponsors: Reps. Don Bacon of Nebraska, Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida, Joe Wilson of South Carolina, and Morgan Luttrell of Texas. It also has the backing of Rep. Kevin Kiley, a Republican-turned-independent from California.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“Thousands of Afghans risked their lives alongside American troops because our country made them a promise: We would not abandon them,” Liccardo said. “Now, we risk sending them back into the hands of the very Taliban forces they helped us fight. This cannot wait until the Democratic majority takes over.”
The bill has the backing of more than 50 organizations, including Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America, Veterans of Foreign Wars and Amnesty International USA.

Once rare, discharge petitions have been successful several times in the 119th Congress as a small number of Republicans have bucked party leadership to join Democrats in getting measures to the floor.

In April, the House voted to reinstate temporary protection for Haitian immigrants after a few Republicans joined with Democrats on that discharge petition. The legislation passed 224-204, with 10 Republicans joining all Democrats in support. While the White House had vowed that Trump would veto the bill, Senate Republicans blocked the legislation from going to his desk.

Other successful discharge petitions have included votes on aid to Ukraine, extending Affordable Care Act subsidies and the Epstein Files Transparency Act put forth by Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif.
The House is scheduled to be in town this week and next before a Thanksgiving recess.

title: FDA orders new warning on GLP-1s over rare eye condition linked to sudden blindness
summary: The Food and Drug Administration said Monday that GLP-1 drugmakers must add a warning label about a rare eye condition that can cause sudden blindness.
story: The Food and Drug Administration said Monday that GLP-1 drugmakers must add a warning label about a rare eye condition that can cause sudden blindness.

The condition, called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NAION, affects the optic nerve, which carries signals from the eye to the brain. When blood flow to the nerve is reduced or blocked, it can cause sudden vision loss. The condition is permanent with no known treatment.
The FDA said “there is a potential increased risk of rare NAION” in people taking GLP-1 drugs.
The agency’s requirement applies to all GLP-1s, including Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Wegovy and Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro and Zepbound, as well as several older GLP-1 diabetes medications.
Spokespeople for both Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly said patient safety is their top priority.
Previous research has found that GLP-1 use may increase the risk of NAION, and Lilly has said it was aware of studies on the potential link.

The FDA said it began looking into a possible link after a 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology that found diabetes patients prescribed semaglutide were four times as likely to develop NAION as those not prescribed the drug.

The agency said it reviewed reports of side effects submitted to its adverse event monitoring system and analyzed data from multiple clinical trials. Cases of NAION have been reported for all currently marketed GLP-1 drugs, the FDA found. However, FDA scientists were not able to identify a mechanism for how the drugs could increase the risk of the eye condition.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Risk factors for NAION can overlap with conditions seen in people taking GLP-1 drugs, including Type 2 diabetes, sleep apnea and hypertension.
NAION is the second most common optic nerve disease in the U.S., occurring in up to 10 out of 100,000 people over age 50, according to the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

“Patients and caregivers should be aware of a potential increased risk of NAION, a rare condition that can result in acute, painless, decreased vision in one eye, including permanent vision loss,” with GLP-1 use, the FDA said in the release.
The drug labels from Novo Nordisk and Lilly also carry other warnings, including for pancreatitis, gallbladder problems and kidney injury.
The labels also carry a black box warning — the FDA’s strongest safety warning — about a possible risk of thyroid tumors.

title: Slotkin lawyer warns Blanche not to obey Trump’s ‘frivolous’ demand to investigate her
summary: Donald Trump told the DOJ to investigate Elissa Slotkin. Her lawyer is lawyer warns Todd Blanche not to obey.
story: WASHINGTON — An attorney for Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin is warning Attorney General Todd Blanche not to bow to President Donald Trump’s demand for a criminal investigation into her political speech.

Over the weekend, Trump posted on his social media platform that he was demanding the Justice Department look into the Michigan senator’s recent comments about how Democratic investigations into the Trump administration could send a “deterrence message” to young people thinking about joining the administration in its final two years.
“By copy of this statement, I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!” Trump wrote.

In a letter to Blanche made public Monday, Preet Bharara, the former U.S. attorney in the Southern District of New York, wrote that it “should not be hard to make clear that we do not live in an authoritarian regime where mere criticism of the powerful can land anyone in legal peril and possibly prison.”
“That requires a clear and public statement confirming that the Department will not pursue this investigation against Senator Slotkin,” he wrote.
The Justice Department didn’t comment on Trump’s post.

The attorney general is appointed by the president and is a member of his Cabinet, but it’s still highly unusual for the White House to publicly demand an investigation. The Justice Department has long sought to separate politics from the law. But under Blanche, Trump’s former personal attorney, the department has investigated many of the president’s perceived political enemies.
For Subscribers
Slotkin, a former CIA and Defense Department official, was also one of a group of lawmakers the Trump administration tried and failed to indict earlier this year over a social media video.

A few weeks before the midterm elections, where the GOP saw massive losses, she spoke at the University of Chicago, arguing that Democrats should focus investigative efforts on those who enable Trump. She said she hoped to deter young people coming out of school from joining the administration.
“I want them to be like, ‘Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don’t want, and so let me avoid participating in that,’” Slotkin said. “I want that deterrence message sent.”

In his post on Truth Social over the weekend, Trump accused Slotkin of “going to go after all young people that believe in Republican Values, and that give even the slightest inclination to be a Republican.”
For Subscribers
Trump’s demand came weeks after Trump ally Mike Davis requested that Harmeet Dhillon — who has since resigned as head of the Civil Rights Division — launch an investigation of Slotkin.
Bharara wrote that Slotkin’s comments were “entirely lawful” and protected by the First Amendment as well as the “speech and debate” clause of the Constitution, which protects members of Congress.

“There is no conceivable basis to investigate the Senator for reminding members of the executive branch who aid the President’s law breaking that there will be accountability for their actions, or expressing the hope that Americans decline to serve in an administration where leaders may ask them to violate the law or misuse taxpayer dollars,” Bharara wrote. “Indeed, the Senator’s statement reinforces the rule of law.”
Bharara asked Blanche to publicly decline to follow Trump’s command.
“The Department should stop threatening our constitutional freedoms and make clear that you will not again launch another frivolous investigation at the taxpayers’ expense,” he wrote.
The Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Bharara’s letter noted that it had been less than a year since the administration failed to indict Slotkin and five other members of Congress over a social media video that reminded members of the military and intelligence communities of their duties not to follow unlawful orders.

“Thankfully, the anonymous citizens of a Washington D.C. grand jury unanimously rejected the Department’s attempt to punish a perceived political adversary for her lawful — indeed, constitutionally privileged — speech,” Bharara wrote.

title: Supreme Court set to pare back federal inmates’ ability to sue officials
summary: The Supreme Court appears likely to bar prison inmates from suing government officials who deny them medical treatment.
story: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Monday appeared likely to bar federal prison inmates from suing officials who deny them medical treatment in the latest case seeking to roll back the ability to hold federal officials accountable for alleged constitutional violations.

The court heard oral arguments over a claim brought by a former federal prison inmate, Kekai Watanabe, who alleges he was denied medical treatment by officers at a Honolulu-based facility in July 2021 after he was beaten by other prisoners during a gang riot.

The case focuses on the scope of a 1971 Supreme Court ruling called Bivens v. Six Unknown Fed. Narcotics Agents, which for the first time allowed people to sue federal officials, including prison officials, for civil rights violations.
The Trump administration’s recent immigration crackdowns have again put the spotlight on the lack of avenues for accountability for agents who face accusations of violating the Constitution.
In Monday’s arguments, the court appeared likely to continue with its recent line of cases that have pared back so-called Bivens claims.

Although the court may not overturn the Bivens decision itself, it seems likely to nullify a 1980 Supreme Court ruling that expanded on it, called Carlson v. Green. Then, the justices said federal prison inmates could sue officials for deliberate indifference to their medical needs under the Constitution’s Eighth Amendment, which protects against cruel and unusual punishment.
That ruling applies only to federal prison inmates, not those in state prisons who have other ways to bring such claims.

In Monday’s argument, several justices in the 6-3 conservative majority pointed out that inmates have other means of seeking redress, including under internal prison procedures and via a federal law called the Federal Tort Claims Act. Under the FTCA, plaintiffs sue the federal government rather than individual officials, and the amount of damages they can win is limited.
Conservative Justice Samuel Alito questioned whether Bivens claims provide “anything of value” because most plaintiffs also bring FTCA claims.
Fellow conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh noted that a “big theme” in the case was that the FTCA provided the necessary remedy for inmates like Watanabe.
“If that’s true, that does seem to negate the need” for Bivens claims in the prisons context, he added.

The court’s most recent decision rolling back Bivens claims was a 6-3 decision in 2022 that said Border Patrol agents could not be sued. A 2023 NBC News investigation found that the ruling had a major impact on ongoing cases around the country, playing a role in 195 cases being dismissed.
For Subscribers

The Bivens decision is on such weak ground that the lawyers for the prison worker in Watanabe’s case, nurse Francis Nielsen, asked the justices to overturn it altogether. The Trump administration filed a brief backing the defendant, but did not ask for the Bivens ruling to be overturned.
For Subscribers
Both Kavanaugh and Chief Justice John Roberts, who were in the majority in the 2022 ruling related to Border Patrol agents, appeared reluctant to overturn Bivens itself in Watanabe’s case.
Roberts seemed inclined to give weight to the Justice Department’s arguments, saying it was a “cautious, incremental approach to such a fundamental question.”

Kavanaugh said a dispute over the medical treatment of a prison inmate would be an “odd case” to use as a vehicle to overturn Bivens; the original case involved federal agents involved in a search of a man’s apartment.
In the incident at the center of Monday’s case, Watanabe said he asked Nielsen to be treated after complaining about pain following the riot but that the request was denied.

Watanabe, who is no longer in federal prison, was later diagnosed with a fractured coccyx and was found to have bone chips embedded in surrounding soft tissue. He then sued, claiming that his Eighth Amendment rights were violated.
A federal court rejected Watanabe’s lawsuit, but the San Francisco-based 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals revived it in a September 2024 ruling.

The original Bivens case arose because Congress has never specifically enacted legislation allowing federal officials to face the same kind of civil rights claims that local and state officials regularly deal with. Although legislation has been proposed in Congress, it has yet to gain any momentum.

title: College Football Playoff is expanding to 24 teams in 2027
summary: The College Football Playoff is expanding once again.
story: The College Football Playoff is expanding once again.

The CFP will switch to a 24-team format for the 2027 season, the organization announced Monday. The new playoffs will double the number of postseason teams from the current format, the 12-team playoff, which began in 2024.

Under the 24-team field, each Power 4 conference champion will receive an automatic bid. There will be 19 at-large bids, and an auto-bid for the highest-ranked Group of 6 school. (The Group of 6 consists of the the American Athletic, Sun Belt, Mid-America, Mountain West, and Pac-12 conferences, as well Conference USA.)
The top 25 teams will still be ranked by the CFP selection committee.

The Power 4 — which includes the Big Ten, SEC, ACC and Big 12 — will no longer host conference championships under the new rules. Instead, their champions will be determined by regular season standings and conference-determined tiebreakers.

In the new format, the top eight teams will receive first-round byes. Teams ranked nine through 16 will host those ranked 17 through 24 at their own stadiums to begin the playoffs, with the second round also taking place on campus, bringing the total number of games played at home stadiums to 16.
The quarterfinals and semifinals will still take place at the New Year’s six bowls, the Rose, Fiesta, Sugar, Orange, Peach and Cotton bowls.

“The decision to expand was driven by a desire to increase opportunities for FBS programs, student-athletes and fan bases to participate in the Playoff and have a chance to play for the CFP National Championship, while new scheduling standards incentivize institutions to schedule more compelling non-conference matchups during the regular season,” the CFP said in a statement.

As a result of the new format, the annual Army-Navy game will be moved to what used to be conference championship week, typically the first Saturday in December. There will be no other games scheduled for that day.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The CFP was first introduced in 2014, when only four teams made the postseason. The four-team playoff was in effect through 2023, after which the field tripled to 12 teams. After only three seasons of the 12-team format, the CFP will soon have six times the number of teams than when it first began.
No format has been able to avoid controversy so far.

In 2023, for example, the last year of the four-team format, an undefeated Florida State team was omitted from the playoff after a late-season injury to its starting quarterback — the first time an undefeated Power 4 school was left out of the postseason.
Last year, Notre Dame was left out of the playoff in the committee’s final ranking, falling below Miami after leading the Hurricanes in every ranking until the ultimate one.
Next year’s college football regular season will begin the week before Labor Day, on the weekend previously known as Week 0. The regular season will conclude on the final weekend of November.
The 24-team format will be in place for at least five seasons, beginning next year through the 2031-32 season.

title: Nvidia stock falls after company opens probe into CEO’s relationship with Chinese spy
summary: Nvidia’s stock slid after the company announced that it had opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.
story: Nvidia’s stock slid about 5% on Monday after the company announced that it had opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman that U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy.

The probe has the potential to unsettle the entire AI boom, fueled by trillions of dollars of spending and investments, in part to purchase Nvidia’s cutting-edge AI chips. Nvidia’s drop wiped out more than $240 billion in value.

The CEO, who also founded the company more than three decades ago, admitted in a note to employees he had been unfaithful to his wife. “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” Huang’s email also said.
For Subscribers

In recent days, the Financial Times and The New York Times reported that Huang had a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman named Alice Huang. A person with knowledge of the matter told NBC News that U.S. intelligence agencies had determined that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. The two Huangs are unrelated.
China has dismissed the espionage allegations as a “smears.” The company where Alice Huang allegedly works, Megaspeed, did not return requests for comment.

Nvidia said in a Sunday statement that independent directors and counsel will oversee the probe. “The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said.
An Nvidia spokesperson told NBC News that Huang was “committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.”
For Subscribers

Despite Nvidia’s importance to the AI trade, the news affected almost no other stocks. The Nasdaq 100, which tracks the top tech stocks at the Nasdaq exchange, soared 3.3%. The broader S&P 500 rose 2.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose more than 1,000 points. Stocks were also propelled higher by a sharp 5% drop in oil prices on Monday, on news that U.S. and Iran talks were continuing. Trump also told CNN on Sunday that it would be “highly unlikely” that he would restart major combat operations against Iran.
Nvidia’s peers, such as AMD, Qualcomm, Taiwan Semi and Intel, all rose along with the broader market. Nvidia was the biggest loser on the Dow and S&P 500.

Before the Huang revelations, the tech industry was on edge, with every headline about AI-linked companies sending stocks either soaring or tumbling. Just last week, tech stocks surged after it became clear on Election Night that the Democrats would win majorities in Congress. But stocks plunged the next day. On Thursday, stocks suffered their worst one-day drop since Trump rocked the global economy with his initial wave of tariffs in April 2025.
Given that there are few more important companies to the tech sector overall, investors and even market watchers not invested in Nvidia shares will be closely following the investigation.

There are still many unanswered questions. On Sunday, Nvidia’s board said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.” But, it did not provide a timeline related to how fast the probe would be conducted or any other details about Huang’s contact with Alice Huang.
Jensen Huang’s influence

Jensen Huang has become one of the main forces driving the global AI push while steering Nvidia to a market value of more than $4 trillion. Huang has led Nvidia since he founded it in 1993, so it would be a seismic change if he were to leave the role.

Huang is the largest individual holder of shares, outside of investment funds, and he is not protected from removal if the board decides to do so. His stake in shares of Nvidia are worth about 3.5% of its shares outstanding, but unlike other major tech firms like Meta, Nvidia has just one class of shares.
Trump on Sunday gave Huang his support, which likely reduces the chance that he is removed as CEO in the near term. “I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what is going on.”
The president was asked if Huang should remain CEO of Nvidia, to which he replied: “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”
With so many outstanding questions about the Huang scandal, few major analysts that cover Nvidia had weighed in on Monday morning about what it could mean for the company’s future.
But those who did said it was a blemish on an otherwise sterling track record, which could spark even more investigations.

“This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons,” wrote Dan Ives, of Yorkville Ives. “There is clearly risk that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the Board investigation and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally.”
Chip analyst Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein Research summed up the gravity of the revelations: “NVIDIA is not an ordinary company and Jensen is not an ordinary CEO; he IS NVIDIA.”

title: Biden says Trump’s Jan. 6 actions ‘should follow him to his grave’
summary: Former President Joe Biden issued scathing criticism of President Donald Trump in his forthcoming memoir, saying his actions during the Jan.
story: Former President Joe Biden issued scathing criticism of President Donald Trump in his forthcoming memoir, saying his actions during the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol “should follow him to his grave.”
Biden’s comments, published as a book excerpt in The Atlantic on Monday, mark some of his strongest criticism of Trump since the former president left office.
In the excerpt, Biden says Trump “led an insurrection” and slammed his decision to issue sweeping pardons of Jan. 6 defendants.
“The criminals who attacked law-enforcement officers that day didn’t deserve pardons,” Biden wrote. “They deserved prison terms.”
The former president added that Trump and the president’s supporters “continue to preen and posture like they’re supporters of law enforcement.”

“Here’s my view: You don’t get to turn a blind eye to cops being punched, speared, sprayed, and brutalized and call yourself a friend of law enforcement,” he wrote. “What Trump did on January 6, 2021, should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Reached for comment, White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis called Biden “the worst president in American history.” She pointed to his handling of the border, crime and inflation, adding, “What they did to this country should never be forgotten.”
The memoir, “Promise Me, America,” is set to be published on Nov. 17.

In a September interview with Time magazine, Trump acknowledged that he was considering pardoning members of his administration before his term concluded, pointing to Biden’s decision to issue preemptive pardons.

Biden issued those pardons to his son, Hunter Biden, and other members of his family, lawmakers on the congressional Jan. 6 committee, Dr. Anthony Fauci, and former Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Mark Milley.
Biden also described his meeting with Trump after the 2024 election, part of a tradition where the outgoing president briefs the incoming president.

Biden said that Trump’s tone “bordered on fawning” and said that Trump told him that “if it weren’t for politics, I believe we’d be good friends” — a remark that the former president said left him “too stunned to respond.”

“He said my performance on job creation had been ‘extraordinary,’” Biden wrote. “He added that he’d been relieved he didn’t have to run against me. I didn’t really understand why he was buttering me up, so I cut off his compliments to move on to the business at hand.”
During the approximately two hour meeting, Biden said that he wanted to give Trump an overview of world issues that he believed would “dominate his presidency.”

“He nodded appreciatively,” Biden said of Trump. “But I noticed a curious pattern: He focused on the personalities of the leaders, as if we were sharing gossip about people at a dinner party, not discussing issues of global significance.”
Biden announced Sunday that he would not “be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped,” pointing to his fight against cancer.
“Some days are better than others,” Biden said in the post to X. “It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down.”

title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assaults
summary: British comedian and actor Russell Brand was in court for sentencing on Monday, days after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault.
story: LONDON — British comedian and actor Russell Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault by a London court on Monday.
The lengthy prison term completes a stunning fall from grace for Brand, 51, who found fame on both sides of the Atlantic chronicling his promiscuity and battles with addiction.
He was found guilty Thursday of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He had pleaded not guilty to all counts and denied all of the allegations.

Brand appeared in the London court Monday wearing a dark suit and at times making a sign of the cross, as the judge, Justice Joel Bennathan, called him a “sexual predator” before delivering his sentence. The judge had warned last week that Brand faced a “significant” prison term for his crimes.
Stressing that he had to be careful not to punish Brand more “because you are famous,” the judge also paid tribute to the “determination and bravery” of the women who testified against him.

“Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent,” he added.
Under English law, the maximum sentence for rape is life imprisonment, and 10 years for one count of sexual assault, according to Britain’s sentencing council.
Brand’s female victims told the court Monday — in person and in written statements — that they were still living with the trauma and effects in their daily lives.

“I’ve been in shock and turmoil for years,” one woman told the sentencing hearing, while another said he appeared to show “no remorse.” Victims of alleged sexual offenses are granted anonymity for life under British law.
Since Brand’s conviction, London’s Metropolitan Police said it had provided prosecutors with investigations into two more rape allegations against him.

Asked by reporters whether he had a message for the victims as he left court, Brand’s father Ron Brand said he didn’t care about them and suggested they had “chased and harassed” his son. He added that he didn’t believe in the justice system “on the basis of what I just watched.”
Brand’s case has renewed scrutiny on the ethics of the entertainment industry, through which Brand rose from a flamboyant British broadcaster and stand-up comedian to a star of Hollywood movies.

title: Talking Shop with Poppi founder Allison Ellsworth about her new beverage brand, Jetty
summary: Poppi founder Allison Ellsworth just launched Jetty, a hydration brand that sells drinks and powders. She gave NBC Selected a behind-the-scenes look into building it.
story: Poppi co-founder Allison Ellsworth knows what you’re thinking: Why would she start another beverage brand after a wildly successful $1.95 billion exit last year? She jokes that she could have retired, but she saw a need her expertise could fill, and she wanted to disrupt the hydration market the same way Poppi redefined how people think of soda.

Meet Jetty, which makes its official debut today on its website, Amazon and Target, as well as in Whole Foods stores nationwide. It sells ready-to-drink bottles and ready-to-mix electrolyte powders, but it’s not a sports drink, and it’s not that sodium-heavy stuff made for athletes.

“When we started looking at it, we realized that hydration products are made for extremes. They’re for sports and they’re so intense — there was nothing for just simply living,” says Ellsworth, who is the brand’s co-founder and chief brand officer alongside Stephen Ellsworth, her husband, as co-founder and CEO. “We formulated Jetty as close to coconut water — nature’s hydration — as possible without that crazy coconut water taste.”

Right before it launched, I talked to Ellsworth about building Jetty, and the lessons she learned during her time at Poppi that she’s applying to running her new company. I also asked her about the products that keep her going throughout her very busy days.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Jetty Orange Mango Electrolyte Drink

Jetty’s drinks and powders come in five flavors, and Ellsworth’s current favorite is orange mango. “We never had a mango flavor at Poppi, so it was one of the first flavors we formulated for Jetty,” she says. “Orange-flavored products can get really Emergen-C tasting — that’s exactly what I didn’t want. I wanted something fresh, tropical, chuggable and refreshing, which is what it is.”

While Ellsworth is excited for customers to finally drink Jetty, she’s equally looking forward to interacting with them online. She took big swings with Poppi to create engaging social media moments that made customers want to buy the products. She also never shied away from making Poppi a founder-led brand. You’ve probably seen her go viral on social media: To date, she has hundreds of thousands of followers across TikTok and Instagram.

With Jetty, Ellsworth is following a similar playbook, but she started amassing a loyal customer base before anyone got to try the drinks and powders. Prior to launch, customers began following the brand’s social media accounts and signing up for its SMS and email lists for a chance to win a J-Card, a.k.a. an American Express Black Card, but for Jetty.

“We had this really unique opportunity to market a product before its launch, and build hype behind it that you can only capture once,” says Ellswoth. “We saw all this data about how people want physical things, which led to the J-Card. It’s an actual card that we’re giving away a limited amount of per year, and people already signed up to get one. It will give them access to stuff nobody else has, like early access to product drops, pop ups, deals and swag. We’re looking at it as a way to build ride-or-die customers from the beginning because at the end of the day, they’re your community.”
To enter to win a J-Card, sign up for Jetty’s email and SMS list — the brand is randomly picking people on a rolling basis.
Therabody Theraface Depuffing Wand

As a now two-time founder launching and promoting a brand-new business while raising three young sons, Ellsworth relies on a few key products to keep her going. “I’m very into beauty and longevity, especially with how much I’m traveling,” she says. “The TheraFace is such a hack, and I love when it gets cold for my under eyes. If I’m traveling and I’m up late, it’s the only thing that makes me look and feel better. A lot of times you have to freeze facial rollers before using them, but when I’m traveling, I obviously don’t have a freezer with me, so the TheraFace is so much easier and works better.”
Yise Beauty Your Favorite Ex Exfoliating Pads

“Yise from Molly Sims has these pads for your face that have transformed my skin,” says Ellsworth. “They’ve gotten rid of my acne and dark spots, and brightened my skin. I just started using them in the last two months, and I absolutely won’t leave the house without them now.”
We can help you find
Rhode Peptide Lip Treatment
“I always need to have a good lip,” says Ellsworth. “I can have no makeup on, but I need to put on my Rhode Peptide Lip, and I have a Laura Mercier lip gloss that I love, too.”
Orion Sleep System

“The one thing that I’m probably the most obsessed with is my Orion sleep system,” says Ellsworth. “It’s basically like an Oura Ring for your body. It’s a pad that goes on top of your mattress, and the temperature changes with your sleep cycle, so if you start to heat up, it cools down. It helps keep you in REM sleep longer, and then it measures your sleep score. When I’m traveling and I don’t have it, I’ll wake up in the middle of the night sweating and I’m like, I miss my Orion.”
Solely Organic Mango Fruit Jerky

Ellsworth’s favorite snack when she’s on the go? “I love Solely’s fruit jerky, because not only can I eat it, but my kids can eat it, too,” she says. “It’s real — you don’t feel like you’re eating gummies full of red dye 40.”

Ellsworth also reaches for Chomps to get some protein in, but there’s one thing she craves most of all. “For better or for worse, my favorite food in the entire world is a good salt and vinegar chip, like a Miss Vickie’s, and string cheese,” she says. “You’ve got your beef stick, cheese, fruit jerky and chips — that’s all your nutrients right there. It’s my girl dinner.”

title: 25+ gifts for dads — even the ones who say they don’t need anything

And as a dad, I have heard that dads, myself included, can be a real pain to get gifts for. I get it. When people ask me what I want, I usually say “I’m good” or come back days later with some hyper-specific item like a 100-watt USB-C cord or a really particular bike bottle.

While I can’t read the minds of every dad, I’ve written gift guides for years, and have collected gift ideas across all sorts of categories, including products I’ve gifted my dad in the past. The NBC Selected team has also tested hundreds (if not thousands) of products over the past year and gifted many to the dads in their lives. With their recommendations, my own dad expertise and advice from fathers that we all know, I crafted this list of the best gifts for dads, including picks in tech, travel, fitness, food and more.

The best gifts for dad in 2026
I curated this list of the best gifts for dads from products our team of shopping experts at NBC Selected have tested over the years, as well suggestions from dads in our lives.
Best tech gifts for dad
Hatch Sleep Clock

Hatch, which makes some of our favorite sleep products, launched a contactless sleep tracker to help with personalizing a bedtime routine. We love that it requires no subscription and includes a 30-night bedside trial.
This sleep clock functions as a sunrise alarm clock and a sound machine, too.
AirPods 5

Apple’s new AirPods 5 are a great gift for dads who wants noise cancellation in a sleek package. They have up to 1.5 times more active noise cancellation than the last generation, and adaptive audio switches between noise cancelling and transparency modes. They’re also sweat- and water-resistant, and they come with hands-free Siri and real-time Live Translation.

NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans tested a pair she received from the brand and says they’re perfect for any busy parents who want to take time for themselves even when they’re home. “I love how crisp the ambient sound is when ANC is turned off; I would imagine for parents who want to tune in and out of their music or podcast to check on the kids or household can appreciate that.”
JBL Clip 5 Portable Bluetooth Speaker

If your father figure is looking for the best outdoor speaker, you should give them the JBL Clip 5. It has a built-in carabiner that lets him attach it to almost anything: a backpack, luggage, exercise bike, shower curtain rod, golf bag, the list goes on. It’s also IP67 water and dust proof, according to the brand — we’ve used it at the beach and pool parties with no problem.
We can help you find
Amazon Kindle Scribe

The Kindle Scribe is part e-reader, part notebook — perfect for dads who like to write notes in the margins of novels and documents. Like other Kindles, it’s excellent for reading since it has a bright, glare-free screen and up to 12 weeks of battery life. Plus, it comes with a stylus, which NBC Selected editors found responsive and as easy as writing on paper when taking notes, signing documents and more.
Best travel gifts for dad
L.L. Bean Boat and Tote

This is one of our favorite everything bags — it’s a weekender, beach bag, grocery tote, whatever he needs. “This may be the greatest thing I received all year,” says Evans, who got it as a gift at an event. “I didn’t think I could be excited about another tote bag, but this one surprised me. The quality is top tier and I actually use it all the time.” You can personalize the tote with a monogram or name up to ten characters long (just plan for extra shipping time). It comes in four sizes with two strap lengths, as well as a zippered top version.
Apple iPad 11-inch

“I wasn’t an ‘iPad person’ until I got one last year — it’s become my favorite travel companion, especially on long flights,” says NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez. He can easily prop it on the seat-back tray table and watch movies and TV shows in-flight. This 11-inch version has an A16 chip that makes connectivity faster, more advanced cameras than the previous model, an all-day battery life.
Yeti Rambler 30-Ounce Tumbler

This Yeti Rambler is one of our go-to tumblers; it’s a double-wall vacuum insulated cup that can keep drinks the right temperature for hours. If you purchase one through Yeti’s site, you can customize the tumbler with personalized text, monogram or imagery for an additional fee. “My dad must have at least a dozen customized Yetis at this point,” says NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin. “When he moved, he carefully wrapped and packed each one like a prized possession.”
Dagne Dover Landon Carryall Bag

This large duffel bag is made from neoprene fabric that’s water resistant, insulating and shock-absorbent, according to the brand. It comes in over ten colors and four sizes. It’s a great gift for dads who take a lot of quick trips for work, or goes to the gym and wants a nice-looking bag that he can take straight to the office.
Apple AirTag 2nd Gen

I’ve gifted my parents (and others) this Apple AirTag for the holidays, and they always manage to find a good use for it. It’s a Bluetooth tracker that uses Apple’s FindMy app to show its precise location. The AirTag has found many a lost keyring, crossbody bag and more in my parent’s house. It doesn’t come with a case, however. If they want to attach it to luggage or a backpack, consider adding something like this Belkin AirTag holder to their gift.
Field Notes: National Parks Series

I’ve used Field Notes memo books for years to take notes, both at work and at home. They’re just small enough to fit into any bag or back pocket, and have quality paper that doesn’t bleed through to the other side. Each book has beautiful cover art of U.S. national parks, though you can also get dad a plain black version.
Best home gifts for dad
ExcelMark Custom Nameplate

“I love the old-fashioned charm this nameplate adds to my desk,” says Fernandez. You can personalize the text, subtext and color, with gold and silver options for the plating. The personalization process takes a few days so make sure you build in enough time to customize and ship it.
Loop Eclipse Sleep Mask

If he has a hard time falling (and staying) asleep because of noise, we highly recommend Loop’s new eye mask — it can be especially helpful if he’s trying to sleep soundly through busy city noise or airplane engine hum. It offers advanced light blocking without putting unwanted pressure on the face, according to the brand, and you can customize the fit. It’s also washable, so you can use it daily.
Amazon Gift Card

I’ve never been disappointed to receive an Amazon gift card as a present. Every dad I know (myself included) is constantly buying little necessities and luxuries from the storefront, and seeing a gift fund balance on my account always sparks joy and gratitude for the person who made that happen. The gift card is available as a physical card or a digital code.
Best fitness gifts for dad
Theragun Relief Massage Gun

Every time I’ve gifted someone a massage gun, everyone in the group wants to try it out. Theragun makes some of our favorites, and this one has a triangle-shaped handle that makes it easy for me to reach tricky spots like my shoulder blades and mid-back. It’s also simple to use for dads who don’t like fussy gadgets: there’s one button that turns it on, off and changes the massage speed.
Brooks Men’s Ghost 18

The Brooks Ghost sneakers are some of NBC Selected editors’ favorite shoes for walking and running — and the Ghost 18 sneakers are a go-to for anyone looking for a comfortable, stable fit. They have breathable upper liners, nitrogen-infused v3 foam for superior shock absorption and a flat-knit tongue for top-of-the-foot protection. It’s available up to size 15 and comes in narrow, wide and extra-wide widths to suit a range of dad sizes.
Best apparel gifts for dad
Carhartt Knit Cuffed Beanie

I’ve given and received so many Carhartt beanies over the years, and I’m always excited to add a new color to my collection. It’s made of acrylic rib knit and has a fold-up cuff design with the Carhartt logo front and center. It comes in one universal size and more than a dozen colors.
Blundstone 587 Round Toe Chelsea Boot

In the winter, the thermal version of these boots are basically my second skin — always on my feet and ready for anything. They pair well with almost any outfit, and are so much easier to pull on and off than any other boot I own. The shoe is made with water-resistant leather and has a cushioned midsole for added comfort.
Mark Diesel Trucker Hat

Whether the closest thing he’ll get to riding a tractor is in virtual reality, or he’s just a guy (likely a millennial) who likes a trucker hat, he could appreciate this snapback from CAT. Evans has this hat and she loves that she can adjust the fit for her small head. She’s a fan of hats from the brand overall, saying that they remind her of her college. “I also love the Payday hat, so much so, I’m planning to get one for my husband so we can twin — even if it’s against his will,” sahe says.
Best kitchen gifts for dad
Asaya Apron with Pockets and Bottle Opener

Most of us know a dad who doesn’t need sunny summer weather to fire up his grill. He may even dominate the kitchen regularly, or love to deep fry the thanksgiving turkey. Either way, he deserves this stylish and durable apron that comes with pockets to hold his tools and towel, and a bottle opener for his beer. It comes in more than a dozen colors, all with stainless steel accents and adjustable straps. The dads in your life can also use it for other activities besides cooking, like painting or home improvement projects.
Alpha Grillers Grill Tools Set

While grilling tools may feel cliché to buy a dad, there’s a reason why dads who grill still enjoy receiving a great set. This one in particular comes with four 18-inch long-reaching utensils that lets them avoid getting their hands too close to the heat. They’re made of thick and durable stainless steel, not flimsy metals, and each piece is dishwasher safe. So you’ve also given your grill-loving dads the gift of not washing dishes. They’ll be thrilled.
Atlas Coffee Club subscription

If he needs fresh beans or wants to try purposefully ground blends for espresso or pour over, an Atlas Coffee Club subscription is for him. You can gift a three- to 12-month subscription of whole, ground or pod compatible coffee. He can choose to get surprise beans or an email ahead of time that allows him to choose based on his preferences.
Fly By Jing Chili Crisp Bundle

Fly By Jing is one of our favorite AAPI-owned food brands, and with this variety set he’ll get several jars of the chili crips bestsellers, including Sichuan Chili Crisp, a sweet and spicy Zhong Sauce and extra crunchy Chengdu Crunch. “I’m not usually a spicy food person, but putting a little of the Chili Crisp sauce on my eggs, toast or salmon adds a crunch and kick that is just perfect,” says Malin.
Best outdoor gifts for dad
Ember Tumbler 2

Evans swears by this travel mug she recently received from the brand for testing. She loves how it keeps her drinks really hot for a couple of hours, eliminating the need to keep microwaving her coffee. “If your dad or husband is as adamant about making his own coffee as I am, he’ll appreciate this travel tumbler,” she says. “If he’s camping or taking a long train or car ride, he’ll benefit from how long the drink stays at your temperature of choice.”
The slim design makes it cupholder compatible, and the leak- and spill-proof lid is ideal for commuters who may need to throw it into a backpack or workbag during their journey.
Goodr OG Sunglasses

Whether he’s walking, running, hiking, biking or just hanging out on a sunny day, these Goodr sunglasses won’t go flying off his face thanks to the grippy, rubberized finish. “I can wear these sunglasses on 10-mile runs and never have to adjust them,” says Malin. They’re also not very pricey — he won’t have to worry if they get a little beat up in a bag or on a weekend getaway.
Victorinox Swiss Army Huntsman Pocket Knife

My dad has a habit of gifting me pocket knives and multitools, and while I don’t think of myself as a pocket-knife kind of dad, I somehow end up using them almost daily around the house. This multitool from Victorinox tackles lots of jobs around my apartment, including opening packages, cutting bags and tweezing splinters.
Celestron Nature DX 8x42 Binoculars

If he has any interest in birds, wildlife or just spotting faraway buildings and landscapes, this pair of binoculars has helped me handle all three with ease. They’re easy to adjust to your eyes and face shape, in my experience, and easy to handle thanks to the rubber and plastic casing. The lenses have an eight-time magnification and can focus as close as 6.5 feet.
Solo Stove Mesa Tabletop Fire Pit

This tabletop fire pit can help bring a warm focal point to his outdoor space, and is small enough to move and store easily. It’s about seven inches tall and five inches across, and you can personalize it with his favorite sports team or a custom message if purchased directly from Solo Stove (for an additional fee). The stove requires firewood or pellets, which are sold separately.
Birdfy Smart Bird Feeder with Camera

A bird feeder is a great way to get colorful visitors soaring towards Dad’s house. This smart bird feeder automatically records birds as they visit the feeder. The Birdfy app sends a notification when a bird is in view, and he can open it to watch a live video feed, or check saved clips later. title: Supreme Court set to pare back federal inmates’ ability to sue officials
summary: The Supreme Court appears likely to bar prison inmates from suing government officials who deny them medical treatment.
story: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Monday appeared likely to bar federal prison inmates from suing officials who deny them medical treatment in the latest case seeking to roll back the ability to hold federal officials accountable for alleged constitutional violations.

The court heard oral arguments over a claim brought by a former federal prison inmate, Kekai Watanabe, who alleges he was denied medical treatment by officers at a Honolulu-based facility in July 2021 after he was beaten by other prisoners during a gang riot.

The case focuses on the scope of a 1971 Supreme Court ruling called Bivens v. Six Unknown Fed. Narcotics Agents, which for the first time allowed people to sue federal officials, including prison officials, for civil rights violations.
The Trump administration’s recent immigration crackdowns have again put the spotlight on the lack of avenues for accountability for agents who face accusations of violating the Constitution.
In Monday’s arguments, the court appeared likely to continue with its recent line of cases that have pared back so-called Bivens claims.

Although the court may not overturn the Bivens decision itself, it seems likely to nullify a 1980 Supreme Court ruling that expanded on it, called Carlson v. Green. Then, the justices said federal prison inmates could sue officials for deliberate indifference to their medical needs under the Constitution’s Eighth Amendment, which protects against cruel and unusual punishment.
That ruling applies only to federal prison inmates, not those in state prisons who have other ways to bring such claims.

In Monday’s argument, several justices in the 6-3 conservative majority pointed out that inmates have other means of seeking redress, including under internal prison procedures and via a federal law called the Federal Tort Claims Act. Under the FTCA, plaintiffs sue the federal government rather than individual officials, and the amount of damages they can win is limited.
Conservative Justice Samuel Alito questioned whether Bivens claims provide “anything of value” because most plaintiffs also bring FTCA claims.
Fellow conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh noted that a “big theme” in the case was that the FTCA provided the necessary remedy for inmates like Watanabe.
“If that’s true, that does seem to negate the need” for Bivens claims in the prisons context, he added.

The court’s most recent decision rolling back Bivens claims was a 6-3 decision in 2022 that said Border Patrol agents could not be sued. A 2023 NBC News investigation found that the ruling had a major impact on ongoing cases around the country, playing a role in 195 cases being dismissed.
For Subscribers

The Bivens decision is on such weak ground that the lawyers for the prison worker in Watanabe’s case, nurse Francis Nielsen, asked the justices to overturn it altogether. The Trump administration filed a brief backing the defendant, but did not ask for the Bivens ruling to be overturned.
For Subscribers
Both Kavanaugh and Chief Justice John Roberts, who were in the majority in the 2022 ruling related to Border Patrol agents, appeared reluctant to overturn Bivens itself in Watanabe’s case.
Roberts seemed inclined to give weight to the Justice Department’s arguments, saying it was a “cautious, incremental approach to such a fundamental question.”

Kavanaugh said a dispute over the medical treatment of a prison inmate would be an “odd case” to use as a vehicle to overturn Bivens; the original case involved federal agents involved in a search of a man’s apartment.
In the incident at the center of Monday’s case, Watanabe said he asked Nielsen to be treated after complaining about pain following the riot but that the request was denied.

Watanabe, who is no longer in federal prison, was later diagnosed with a fractured coccyx and was found to have bone chips embedded in surrounding soft tissue. He then sued, claiming that his Eighth Amendment rights were violated.
A federal court rejected Watanabe’s lawsuit, but the San Francisco-based 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals revived it in a September 2024 ruling.

The original Bivens case arose because Congress has never specifically enacted legislation allowing federal officials to face the same kind of civil rights claims that local and state officials regularly deal with. Although legislation has been proposed in Congress, it has yet to gain any momentum.

title: Democratic lawmakers seek to restore deportation protections to Afghans in the U.S.
summary: A pair of House Democrats will try to bypass Republican leaders and force a vote to restore Temporary Protected Status to Afghan nationals in the United States by introducing a discharge petition when Congress returns Monday night.
story: A pair of House Democrats will try to bypass Republican leaders and force a vote to restore Temporary Protected Status to Afghan nationals in the United States by introducing a discharge petition when Congress returns Monday night.

Rep. Jason Crow, D-Colo., and Rep. Sam Liccardo, D-Calif., will file the petition, which would require signatures from 218 members to bring forth legislation to grant Afghans protection from deportation until mid-2029.

TPS, created by Congress in 1990, is a Department of Homeland Security program that allows migrants to live and work in the U.S. for up to 18 months if their home countries have been designated as unsafe. The time period can be extended.
President Donald Trump’s administration terminated the status for Afghanistan in May 2025, a designation that former President Joe Biden’s administration had granted in 2022.

“This administration is returning TPS to its original temporary intent,”  then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said at the time. She added that “Afghanistan has had an improved security situation, and its stabilizing economy no longer prevent them from returning to their home country.”
While the Trump administration recently planned to deport dozens of Afghan immigrants and asylum-seekers to Pakistan, a federal judge last week temporarily blocked that move.

Crow and Liccardo would need all current House Democrats and a handful of Republicans to sign on to their discharge petition to reach the necessary 218 signatures. The pair already introduced a special rule on Oct. 1, allowing them to start collecting signatures as soon as they submit the petition on Monday.

“Our Afghan partners put their lives on the line to help protect American servicemembers like me,” Crow, who served as a paratrooper and an Army Ranger in Iraq and Afghanistan, said in a statement. “I’m working to force a vote that will protect Afghans already in the United States because I won’t let our nation leave these brave Afghans behind.”

If Crow and Liccardo are successful in reaching the 218-signature threshold, GOP leaders would be forced to bring forward the Afghanistan TPS Act for a floor vote. That bill, which the pair introduced in July, would grant TPS to Afghans until July 2029. The legislation would need a majority vote on the House floor to pass.

The bill already has four Republican co-sponsors: Reps. Don Bacon of Nebraska, Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida, Joe Wilson of South Carolina, and Morgan Luttrell of Texas. It also has the backing of Rep. Kevin Kiley, a Republican-turned-independent from California.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“Thousands of Afghans risked their lives alongside American troops because our country made them a promise: We would not abandon them,” Liccardo said. “Now, we risk sending them back into the hands of the very Taliban forces they helped us fight. This cannot wait until the Democratic majority takes over.”
The bill has the backing of more than 50 organizations, including Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America, Veterans of Foreign Wars and Amnesty International USA.

Once rare, discharge petitions have been successful several times in the 119th Congress as a small number of Republicans have bucked party leadership to join Democrats in getting measures to the floor.

In April, the House voted to reinstate temporary protection for Haitian immigrants after a few Republicans joined with Democrats on that discharge petition. The legislation passed 224-204, with 10 Republicans joining all Democrats in support. While the White House had vowed that Trump would veto the bill, Senate Republicans blocked the legislation from going to his desk.

Other successful discharge petitions have included votes on aid to Ukraine, extending Affordable Care Act subsidies and the Epstein Files Transparency Act put forth by Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif.
The House is scheduled to be in town this week and next before a Thanksgiving recess.

title: Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about making UFC head Dana White press secretary
summary: The president suggested on Truth Social that White should bring several UFC fighters as assistants.
story: President Donald Trump said he was joking when he offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the CEO and president of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, putting an end to more than 24 hours of speculation about whether the announcement was serious.
“I will tell you, I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea, and there’s only one Dana. He’s great,” Trump told reporters Sunday evening on the tarmac in Palm Beach, Florida.
Trump sent out a surprise post Saturday on Truth Social saying he had offered White the job. The position has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left the role after just five days last month.
“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump wrote.
Trump suggested in his post that White should bring several UFC fighters, including Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje and Amanda Nunes, as assistants to defend against the “Lunatic Left.”
“Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!” he added.
White said at a boxing event in London on Saturday evening that he was heading to Washington that night and had a meeting scheduled with Trump on Monday.
Trump told reporters that the meeting Monday was still on but that it was unrelated to the press secretary position.

“So he’s actually coming tomorrow,” Trump said Sunday night. “Of course, I was kidding. ... But Dana is actually coming tomorrow, actually, for other reasons. I think he was going to be in Washington, so he’s going to come over and see me.”
When Trump posted on Truth Social earlier Saturday, it was unclear whether his offer was a serious one.
Shortly after Trump posted, White posted on Instagram what appears to be an AI-generated image of himself behind the lectern in the White House briefing room, captioned, “On to the next chapter.”
White also added a screenshot of Trump’s post to his Instagram Story.
Trump and White have long been friends, and Trump has attended many UFC fights while he has been in the White House.
White this year also organized a UFC fight on the South Lawn of the White House, an event that was part of a slate commemorating the U.S.’ 250th birthday.
Many Trump administration officials and Republican lawmakers attended the fight in July.
A spokesperson for the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Zacharia replaced Karoline Leavitt, who had been White House press secretary since Trump returned to office in January of last year. Leavitt announced in August that she would leave her post to spend more time with her family.
The White House had another staff shake-up Friday, when chief of staff Susie Wiles said she would step down. Trump named longtime aide Stephen Miller as her replacement.

Wiles’ departure made her the seventh woman to leave the Trump administration this year. So far, all of them have been replaced by men, except Zacharia and Leavitt, as a press secretary has not yet been named.

title: Hoda Kotb Says She Hasn’t Yet Gone Out with the Man She Met on a Plane: ‘I Think I’m Scared’
summary: Hoda Kotb says airplane man has asked her out but they haven’t met yet. Here’s what to know.
story: Jenna Bush Hager is determined to get Hoda Kotb to meet up for coffee with the mystery man Hoda connected with during a flight earlier this year after Hoda said she’s “scared” to take that step.

Hoda shared on TODAY Nov. 9 that she has remained in contact via text with a man she met briefly on a plane in a scene straight out of a rom-com. She said on TODAY in August that the two of them were “both crying” and the conversation was “firing on all cylinders” before the two parted ways after the flight.
Jenna asked Hoda, who was her guest co-host on Nov. 9, for an update on the unnamed man. The two also met again in May during the Cannes Film Festival in France.
More about Hoda's "Airplane Man"
Hoda Kotb’s Love Life Update Has Jenna and Sheinelle Begging for More: ‘What Is Happening?!'Sandra Bullock Pries Hoda Kotb for More Details About Her ‘Connection’ With Man on Plane
Hoda Kotb’s Love Life Update Has Jenna and Sheinelle Begging for More: ‘What Is Happening?!'
Sandra Bullock Pries Hoda Kotb for More Details About Her ‘Connection’ With Man on Plane

“He’s asked me to meet him out a couple times, and I haven’t,” Hoda said. “And I’ll tell you why I haven’t. One, probably I’m scared. Two, I think I like a flirt that you don’t know what it is, but it might be something. And sometimes once you know it isn’t something, then it’s not so fun any more.

“So I think I’m sort of just keeping it as a thing,” she continued. “Truly, if I were to swallow a truth pill right now, I’m 62 years old, I have two young kids, and I believe the love part of my life is a piece that’s coming. I don’t go, ‘Oh well, that’s that.’”
Hoda shares daughters Haley, 9, and Hope, 7, with former partner Joel Schiffman. While she remains single, she is still open to the possibility of love.

“Here’s what I think about my future relationship life because I’ve been thinking about this,” she told Jenna. “I believe that as I am going through life that there is going to be a person who shares more than just the things that mattered to be when I was younger. I want someone like a deep spiritual connection, a deep emotional connection.
“I think that’s coming, and I think I have to take risks to get it,” she added.
Jenna thinks it’s time for one of those risks. She said the next time the man from the plane contacts Hoda, she has to go.
“Because my friend is brave and does things that scare her, so I want you to go on that coffee date,” Jenna said.
“OK,” an emotional Hoda said. “I will go on the coffee date.”
“We have to cry within 30 minutes otherwise it’s not us,” Jenna joked.

title: What Caleb Williams Told 10-Year-Old Podcasters Jimmy V and Hen Dawg at Their First Bears Game
summary: Viral kid podcasters Jimmy V and Hen-Dawg got to meet Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams before and after his team hosted the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
story: It was a dream come true for viral kid podcasters Jimmy V and Hen-Dawg, who got to meet Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams before and after his team hosted the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Nov. 8 on “Sunday Night Football.”
The 10-year-old kids, whose names are Henry “Hen-Dawg” Zotti and Jimmy “V” Maley, are huge Bears fans who were surprised with tickets to the game on TODAY on Nov. 4.

Before the game, they got to walk around Soldier Field with Kaylee Hartung, who surprised them by saying they would head to the field where they walked by an end zone and sat on the “Football Night in America” set. Then, they chatted up Bears kicker Cairo Santos, before the main event: meeting Williams, which they said was their big goal.
“Good to see y’all,” Williams said as he signed autographs for them.
“Are you going to lock in?” Hen-Dawg asked, prompting Williams, who was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, to chuckle.
“Are we your favorite podcasters?” Hen-Dawg then asked.
“Y’all are. I gotta get back to work now,” he said before giving both boys a fist bump.

Come game time, the pair was focused on rooting for the Bears. The Chicago team shook off four interceptions by Williams to win its fourth straight game on the strength of Santos’ walkoff field game to propel them to a 27-24 victory and improve their record to 7-2.
The duo then reconnected with Williams after the game.
“I’m happy y’all could make it,” he told them while signing more autographs. “We got a win for you.”
Jimmy V and Hen-Dawg weren’t quite done yet, either, as they appeared live Nov. 9 on TODAY. For Hen-Dawg, there was no doubt what his favorite part of the night was.
“Meeting Caleb Williams and going on the field at the end of the game,” he said.
“Meeting Caleb was great,” Jimmy V said.
Hartun reminded the boys that Williams had told them their podcast was his favorite.
“Yup,” Jimmy V said simply, while Hen-Dawg later confirmed that Williams did tell them that after the game.
“I’m sure somebody has it on clip,” Jimmy V said about the moment where Williams told them.
While the boys appeared to have a blast, they did have a difference of opinion over one matter: food.
“I had two cheeseburgers, and they were massive, but they were so good,” Jimmy V said, noting the food was “perfect.”
Hen-Dawg said he ate the same thing, “but I didn’t really like it that much.”
The boys will have a chance to cool off for awhile before returning to gameday mode, as the Bears are on a bye week coming up and don’t play again until they host the New Orleans Saints on Nov. 22.

title: ‘Love Is Blind’ Stars Sarah Williams Explains the ‘Really Traumatic’ Reason Her Marriage to John Shannon Ended
summary: Why did Sarah Williams and John Shannon break up after Love Is Blind?
story: Warning: Spoilers from the “Love Is Blind” Season 11 reunion below.
The only couple to say “I do” on Season 11 of “Love Is Blind” has revealed that they divorced a year after tying the knot.

During the Season 11 finale, viewers watched John Shannon and Sarah Williams exchange vows and get married in front of their friends and family. The two were the first couple to get engaged in the pods despite an unusual start. After one of their first dates, Williams overheard Shannon telling another cast member that he didn’t rank her at the top of her list. She mentioned the conversation to John and the two were able to laugh about it. They also had chats in the pods about vaccinations, abortions and the health care industry, in which Williams, a health-care program manager, educated John on her experience caring for others.

On their wedding day, Williams revealed to her family that they had more discussions off-camera about Shannon’s views. She said he shared that he believed single women over 30 were “problematic” and he worried Williams would be a “consumer of politics” who would want to frequently chat about the state of the world. Still, they got married and gushed about their future together to the cameras before they were shown happily dancing at their reception.
But at the reunion, which aired Nov. 8, the couple revealed they broke up.
When co-host Nick Lachey asked what happened since the wedding, Shannon replied, “Unfortunately, Sarah and I are no longer together, which is my fault.”
He added that they had a “wonderful” year of marriage before getting choked up.
“About six months ago, I made a mistake. There was a major breach of trust on my part,” he continued. “It’s hard to talk about.”
